questEffects.text: A local now knows the trick. The pest problem is officially somebody else's competence.

beats.description:
Turns out, agricultural type persons and bugs can get along pretty well if taught how to communicate properly. 

NOW the good people of Lyrenn have an awesome Swarm of Kewl Bugs as a mascot.

You'll get one of the first T shirts as soon as they come out!
beats.memoryText: They taught our people to speak to the swarm. Lyrenn keeps its bugs now — as a mascot, of all things.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Gentle Pest, Violence

questEffects.text: Violence. Against something described, in writing, as gentle. Lyrenn remembers.
The land noticed.

beats.description: That certainly made the bugs scatter and leave. Well done ... ?
beats.memoryText: They drove the burrowers off with force. The channels are quiet. The soil is quieter, and it noticed.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Gentle Pest, Fail
beats.description: The burrowers remain unmoved, the channels remain chewed, and the east field has formed an opinion of you it will share with the rest of the hex by morning. Lyrenn does not boo. Lyrenn remembers.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Field That Remembers You, Quest Acceptance
beats.description: You agreed to walk the low field — the one nobody harvests, where the plants grow in postures and the air says names. Bring nothing sharp. It notices.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Field That Remembers You, Intro
beats.description:
The low field bends under twilight. Not from wind. From posture. Plants rise in shapes that disturb your breath. A stalk hunched like someone mid-apology. A cluster curled inward like hands that almost reached. A blossom tilted away — as if refusing eye contact. When dusk deepens, the field exhales. Names move through it. Softly. Not accusations. Not pleas. Just names. No one harvests here. The earth is speaking in gestures.

At the field's edge, half-buried where the furrows end, a stone figure hunches in exactly the posture of the nearest stalk — mid-apology, hands that almost reach. Either the plants are copying it, or it copied them, and nobody in Lyrenn will say which out loud.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Field that remembers you, burn the field

questEffects.text: The field no longer remembers you. It no longer remembers anything. Great job.
The land noticed.

beats.description:
Flame races too quickly.

The plants scream once.

Then silence.

The air becomes simple again.

Too simple.
beats.memoryText: They burned the low field. The names stopped. The air out there is simple now — too simple.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Field that remembers you, talk to the plants

questEffects.text: You talked to the plants. The plants talked back. Nobody in Lyrenn finds this strange, which is itself strange.

beats.description: You talked to the field the way you'd talk to someone who'd had a hard year — no fixing, no hurry, just company. It worked better than it had any right to. The names come softer out there now, and some of the plants insisted on coming with you, which nobody in Lyrenn has a protocol for and everybody in Lyrenn is quietly thrilled about.
beats.memoryText: They talked to the field like kin. Some of the plants followed them home. The names come softer now.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Forest That Will Not Be Fought, Quest Acceptance
beats.description: You agreed to deal with the treeline that rearranges paths overnight and has started editing the fence line. Local doctrine is in the name: the forest will not be fought.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Field that remembers you, harvest the plants

questEffects.text: Harvested. The field remembers being useful, which is the nicest thing anyone's done for it in years.

beats.description:
The sap tastes like memory.

Bitter.

Familiar.

You can use it to create “Distilled Guilt” - Useful in Courtly Intrigue raid scenarios.
beats.memoryText: They harvested the grieving field. Distilled Guilt sits in the stores; the field is bare.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Forest will not be fought

choices.label: Redirect growth
choices.description: Head 'em up and move 'em out trees! Have we got an AMAZING empty meadow with stunning hillside views and no wrecked highways around for miles! And it's move in ready! All it's missing is you!

choices.label: Force control
choices.description:
Might as well show them what you do to things who try to take what's yours; things that burn, and things that fall easily to the axe.

I realize now that this could apply to many different things, which greatly reduces the emotional impact of the above statement.

God. Dammit.

choices.label: Negotiate space
choices.description: The art of dealmaking, specifically with encroaching technomagical post apocalyptic trees, is something to which you were BORN. You're a natural. You will have these trees drilling into the palms of your hands with their roots in order to obtain sustenance in no time!

choices.label: Do nothing
choices.description: Lyrenn has a LOT of shit going wrong with it huh? Must really suck to live here ... Someone should probably do something about it or something.

choices.label: Show it the Tifaret accord
choices.description: Only meaningful if you have actually made peace with the forest of Early Tifaret — forests talk through the roots, and this one checks references.

beats.description:
The treeline does not advance.

It rearranges.

Paths you walked yesterday bend elsewhere.

Clearings reopen in apology.

Branches lean inward as you speak.

Wind carries tone, not words.

When someone raises their voice, birds scatter.

When someone softens, roots uncoil slightly.

The forest is not aggressive.

It is correcting.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Forest will not be fought, negotiate
beats.politicalTags: politics.redistribution politics.security politics.welfare politics.mutual_aid politics.property_rights politics.order compromise consent

questEffects.text: Space negotiated. The treaty is verbal, binding, and enforced by roots.

beats.description:
After a brief but intense negotiation, you are able to reach an agreement with the forest.

They will retreat to the edge of the town.

In return, the townsfolk will tend them and hold a yearly festival in their honor.

Ok, so the trees are pretty full of themselves.

But they are ALSO full of a pretty awesome magical sap, which they are willing to share.

So, like, win win!
beats.memoryText: A treaty: the forest holds at the town's edge, we tend it and keep a yearly festival, and it shares its sap.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Forest will not be fought, redirect

questEffects.text: Growth redirected. The forest agreed to disagree, in the direction you pointed.

beats.description:
Have you ever seen a forest arguing about who gets to have the window seat? It's quite a thing to behold. But you got the trees to the right place, and Lyrenn is breathing much easier. Hope whoever lives near there likes asshole trees!

One correction from the ridge folk, later: the trees refuse one corner of the meadow. A moss-covered stone figure stands there, and the forest will not root within reach of it.
beats.memoryText: They talked the whole treeline into the meadow past the ridge. Lyrenn breathes easier; the ridge folk inherit opinionated trees.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Forest will not be fought, force

choices.label: Burn it down. Burn it ALL down.
choices.description: Time to let the very soil of the earth know that you mean business, and you will not show weakness. You will burn this forest using magic from a safe distance, which is definitely the strongest, bravest way of doing things. And that's what YOU'RE about.

choices.label: You against a forest. LET'S DO THIS.
choices.description: You can still burn things during hand to hand combat too, don't worry. But this way it's so much easier for you to get hurt or dead. That makes it more fun right? It's like extreme sports?

choices.label: Then again ...
choices.description: You are worried what a tree rumble means for the integrity of your face and vital organs. Maybe think of something else to do. There was a list with some suggestions earlier ...

beats.description: The trees felt you reach the decision before you said it — roots closed around chunks of old highway and lifted them like question marks, waiting to see which weapon you'd choose. The forest will not be fought. It is, however, absolutely willing to demonstrate why.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Forest will not be fought, negotiate (fail)
beats.description:
They shouldn't have called your offer laughable. And they shouldn't have criticized your argument's logical core like that. And making fun of your clothes was really uncalled for.

They could have just said no.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Forest will not be fought, redirect (fail)
beats.description:
I mean, you get it. They JUST moved in. They're not even done unpacking yet. Moving again just sounds like a LOT, you know?

Besides, none of them would look you in the eye, and everyone kept saying "I'll need to check with my partner," like you couldn't tell their partner was standing right there next to them ...

Needless to say, they did not accept your offer.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Forest will not be fought, force (burn)
beats.politicalTags: politics.purge politics.repression politics.property_rights politics.order politics.security politics.welfare coercive domination

questEffects.text: You burned it. The forest will not be fought — but apparently it can be arsoned. Lyrenn remembers.
The land noticed.

beats.description: From your vantage you watch the flames begin. And that is all there is to it.
beats.memoryText: They burned the forest from a distance. It watched them decide to. Lyrenn will pay for that.

beats.label: Lyrenn - The Forest will not be fought, force (fight)

questEffects.text: You fought a forest. Entered a land war with lumber. Results as expected. Lyrenn remembers.
The land noticed.

beats.description:
You will never look at wrecked cars the same every again. When coming at you having been flung by a living trebuchet - it makes an impression. In many different and exciting ways.

Ya that was DUMB. And Lyrenn is going to pay for your arrogance, unfortunately.
beats.memoryText: They fought the trees root-and-fist and were beaten. The forest remembers; Lyrenn will pay for the arrogance.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Mine That Answered Back, Quest Acceptance
beats.description: You agreed to go below. The new shaft broke into something on Level Four, and Foreman Calder — a man not given to poetry — refuses to call it a cavern. The mine answered back. Someone has to decide what Khezek Tor says next.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Mine that answered back

choices.label: Exploit it
choices.description: Yesodium is SUPER useful. NOT continuing would be really stupid. Bad leadership really. Drill baby drill!!!

choices.label: Seal the Breach
choices.description:
Shut that shit DOWN. I'm pretty sure I read somewhere that delving too deeply was BAD.

Options - 

2 OP (any type)

Valuable material

Public vow

choices.label: Open it up fully
choices.description:
Fuck it. Dynamite this bitch. There has to be more magical silence Yesodium shit close by!! It is all be yours!

4 Violence OPs

beats.description:
The new shaft broke into silence.

Not cavern.

Not creature.

Silence.

Tools vibrate in hands before striking.

Rock leans inward.

Miners dream of owing something.

Of signing contracts they do not remember reading.

The ore veins rearrange subtly overnight.

Not randomly.

Like something adjusting posture.

A survey photo pinned in the Maw shows the new shaft's mouth flanked by two upright shapes the caption calls "pillar collapse." Nobody who has seen the photo believes the caption. Nobody has taken the photo down either.
beats.inviteText: Calder wants you below. The new shaft broke into something, and he won't call it a cavern.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Mine that answered back, seal
beats.politicalTags: politics.order politics.security politics.welfare politics.mutual_aid harm_reduction regulation

questEffects.text: Sealed. The mine still answers, but now it's muffled, which everyone agrees to call 'solved'.

beats.description: The seal holds. The rumble is gone; the mountain sits easier, and everyone underground knows who paid for that — the Stewards, out of their own banks, with output down and not one name added to any list. Calder chalked the shift on the Brace ledger himself and underlined nothing, which from Calder is a medal.
beats.memoryText: They paid out of their own banks to seal the breach. Output dipped; nobody died. First clean work I've seen on this mountain.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Mine that answered back, exploit

questEffects.text: Exploited. The mine answers back and you've put it on payroll.
The compound started coughing the week output doubled.
The Brace took the extra load without a word. That's not the same as taking it well.

beats.description: The surplus went two places: the ledgers, and the Allesh-Gilliam Leygate's footings — Khezek ore is shoring up the coalition's front door, and the numbers are genuinely beautiful. The compound's cough went a third place, quieter, bed to bed. Calder keeps the tonnage on one side of his chalk ledger and a list of names on the other, and he has stopped explaining what the second column is for.
beats.memoryText: They doubled output and let the mountain pay for it. Sickness in the compound, the Brace one bad day closer. I'm keeping a list of names.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Mine that answered back, open

questEffects.text: Opened. Whatever was answering has been given the floor.
The deep silence is open, and it is very patient.

beats.description:
Well. This containment sink is no longer containing anything. 

It's quiet at the moment. But you have an open Qlipothic energy sink, that is now slowly morphing into a portal.

+2 darkness ... and maybe rising.
beats.memoryText: They dynamited the deep silence open. The map has a new center now, and it is very patient. I chart the edges of it nightly.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness Sometimes
beats.description: You agreed to look at the shipment problem: Yesodium crates that hum, sometimes, and sour the dreams of whoever hauls them. Quartermaster Brennig's manifest says everything is fine. Quartermaster Brennig's face says the manifest is lying.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness sometimes

choices.label: Standardize
choices.description: Ok, you're starting to get the vibe here. Things are haphazard. They don't have processes. There workflow is suboptimal. They don't have enough stories on their scrum board. The ore doesn't feel valued properly. You can help with this!

choices.label: Rite
choices.description: You think you can see just enough of the problem to nudge it out of the way with a properly formulated rite. A way to communicate directly with the stone, thank it, and frame operations here properly.

choices.label: Ignore
choices.description: It's still ore, ain't it? Maybe if we just harvest MORE of it, we'll get through the tainted bits!

beats.description:
Ore crates from Khezek-Tor hum faintly during transit.

Not ominous.

Unsettled.

When mishandled, arguments erupt nearby.

Lights flicker.

Dreams sour.

The ore isn’t cursed.

It’s improperly framed.
beats.inviteText: Quartermaster Brennig has a crate on the bench that won't stop humming, and a manifest that won't stop lying about it.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness sometimes, standardize

questEffects.text: Standardized. The UTTER DARKNESS now ships with a manifest, which somehow makes it scarier.

beats.description:
You implement a standard sacred handling protocol. 

This slows down your transportation, giving you time to add proper markings and orientation to the shipments.

This costs 3 Economy OP.

And raises morale by 2.
beats.memoryText: Sacred handling protocols on every crate now. Slower, calmer; no more soured dreams riding out with the ore. My manifest finally tells the truth.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness sometimes, rite

questEffects.text: The rite held. The shipment is DARKNESS, sometimes, on a schedule everyone can live with.

beats.description:
You perform a simple rite of orientation and atonement for the stone. It may or may not have involved puppets. The rock has a surprisingly short attention span for a tectonically oriented sentience. But it got the vibe, and understands the goals here.

People are impressed. Word spreads - damn elegant solution, that. Someone who gets mines. 

You made some allies today.

+2 to Morale and Loyalty, -1 to Darkness, +2 to non lethal, soft power, culture, and faith OP banks.
beats.memoryText: Puppets, of all things — but the stone got the vibe. Word went round the galleries: these ones actually get mines.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Shipment of Utter Darkness sometimes, ignore

questEffects.text: Ignored. The shipment question resolved itself, which is never how that works.

beats.description:
The tainted shipments continue. Some folks get sick. The mood in your enclaves dampens a bit.

But the Economy does seem to be getting better.

+2 Economy OPs. -1 morale, +1 darkness
beats.memoryText: The humming crates keep rolling. Some folks got sick. The ledgers have never looked better, and I have never liked them less.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Valhaulan Seal, Quest Acceptance
beats.description: Calder's crews won't work the gallery by the old seal, and Calder doesn't spook. The markings are fresh, precise, and pointed — somebody has been maintaining this thing, recently, and nobody at Khezek Tor is on that shift roster. The coalition is now formally curious.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - Valhaulan Seal Cinematic
beats.description:
The sealed shaft bears Valhaulan sigils.

Recent.

Precise.

Directional.

The seal doesn’t bind inward.

It points outward.

Like a pipe.

Like a siphon.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Valhaulan Seal

choices.label: Restore the seal
choices.description: As best you can figure, the Valhaulans have weaponized the Yeodium's resentment. Then, it was resentment about being left untapped and in potentia. Someone, somewhere, is getting a blast of bad juju. Best reclaim what's yours. And then have a long talk with some Valhaulans.

choices.label: Redirect the seal's energies
choices.description: At least this way you KNOW where you're sending the bad vibes? Hit a hex that you hope isn't populated? That way Khezek-Tor doesn't get hit with all of that bad juju coming back home. That would seriously slow down production.

choices.label: Break the seal
choices.description: What did they seal up to get this thing humming to begin with? Dynamite this mutha! Open it up! let's see what's inside!!

beats.description: The shaft face, up close: Valhaulan sigils laid over older work like a correction in confident handwriting. The seal doesn't bind inward — every line of force points OUT, down the mountain, toward the coast. Whatever debt this rock was made to hold, someone re-addressed the envelope. Three tools are on the table: mend it, aim it, or open it — and the mountain is listening to the discussion.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Valhaulan Seal, restore
beats.politicalTags: politics.mutual_aid politics.welfare politics.order order harm_reduction ritual

questEffects.text: Seal restored — Khezek-Tor keeps the burden.

beats.description:
Khezek-Tor becomes Irradiated for one turn due to the massive re-ingestion of the outsourced energies.

Turns out there was a Valhaulan Sympathizer group in town. They got pissed, made some noise, got collared. That could cause problems later. 

Yesodium mining actually runs steady, so no economic impact.

And you have clearly shown what kind of outfit you are trying to run here.

-2 to darkness. -1 to morale.
beats.memoryText: They took the burden back instead of passing it on. The mine ran hot for a turn and a sympathizer cell got collared. Calder remembers who paid.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Valhaulan Seal, redirect
beats.politicalTags: politics.order politics.security politics.property_rights coercive collective_punishment scapegoat

questEffects.text: Seal redirected — you chose who pays.

beats.description:
You can feel a brief intake of psychic breath, like the fetid breeze off a swamp, as the seal recalls its burden and then redirects it towards your newly chosen target.

The entire region knows you did this.

They worry you might do it again.

They worry it might be them next.

-2 morale, loyalty, +2 darkness

-1 step to relationship with all Faction with whom one is not already Friendly.
beats.memoryText: They aimed the seal at somebody else and the whole coast felt it exhale. Everyone wonders who's next.

beats.label: Khezek-Tor - The Valhaulan Seal, break

questEffects.text: Seal broken.

beats.description: The seal breaks like a promise — quietly, then all at once, then in everyone else's direction. What was held is now headed, coastward, down the same line the survey stations have been shaking about, and every needle on the Triangle wakes up screaming at once. Khezek Tor holds — barely, loudly, at a cost the mountain will be invoicing for years. Nobody dies who didn't volunteer. But the heading is lit now, burning-map bright, and whatever runs supply to that stretch of nothing knows the door just unlocked itself from your side.
beats.memoryText: They broke the seal and read the debt's forwarding address by the light of it. The heading is lit; the coast knows something opened.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Leyline Stabilizer
beats.description:
The Leygate hums like someone pretending they aren’t tired.

Blue flickers yellow.

Yellow flickers blue.

The stabilizer readout shows turbulence.

Not failure.

Persistence.

Avuncular Joan’s key still functions.

One charge remains.

The engineer doesn’t look relieved.

“That’s worse.”

If it misfires, it won’t explode.

It will remember wrong.

“Send the wrong shape of thing.”

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer Negotiation

choices.label: Trade
choices.description:
Pretty sure that you can come to some sort of equitable trading set up. This is their gig. They just want to know who they're dealing with, and if you've come and presented yourselves as you are, or as you might be, or as you were.

Make a persuasion check or spend 2 Soft Power OP.

choices.label: Shared Oversight
choices.description: You know, you ARE new here. There is a working Leygate here at Fixit Farm - they know what they're doing. Setting up a network would be nice. Cozy. Neighborly. Convenient. What about shared oversight of the network?

choices.label: Hard Ask
choices.description: Time to show folks around here that compliance and cooperation with your faction are not optional. They will give it to you. And be thankful that you do not ask for more. Ok you don't SAY that second part out loud, but you say it with your eyes. Actually you find out later that someone was holding up a sign saying it. But right now you don't know that.

choices.label: Delay
choices.description: Why is everyone staring at you? This is fucked up. A lot of pressure right here. Get this wrong and you'll never be able to make a first impression again. Better pretend you mispronounced what you want and actually meant something else and you will check back later.

beats.description:
Mara clicks her thumb in anticipation. "Now this is what we're about. 

What you got as we might want?"

And then she tries REALLY hard to not look interested but instead looks like she's trying really hard to not look interested but is failing badly but doesn't know that she's failing badly.
beats.inviteText: is ready to talk terms on the Leyline Stabilizer.

handoff.text: Mara nods you toward the Arc Bay — Young Gearbox keeps the stabilizer, and he'll be expecting you.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - Trade

questEffects.text: The Leygate part — traded fair.

beats.description:
You conclude your negotiation with a handshake.

You have secured assurances that the Jackalopes will send someone along with the stabilizer who will install it.

You feel, for the first time since arriving in Bad Eden really, not quite entirely unlike a competent person.
beats.memoryText: Traded the replacement Leygate stabilizer part to the Stewards — a deal fairly struck, by Jackalope standards.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - Shared Oversight

questEffects.text: The Leygate part — shared oversight.

beats.description:
You conclude your negotiation with a handshake, and a shot of some harsh orange liquid that tastes strongly of petrichor and fucks you up stright and proper.

You have secured assurances that the Jackalopes will send someone along with the stabilizer who will install it, and help your engineering team get it up and running and calibrated.

You feel, for the first time since arriving in Bad Eden really, slightly competent.
beats.memoryText: Handed the Stewards the Leygate part under shared oversight — Jackalope hands stay on the work, which is how it should be.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - Hard Ask

questEffects.text: The Leygate part — taken on the hard ask.

beats.description:
You firmly explain that the entire region needs this, and will benefit from your ability to easily move about your new command. They don't argue, just quietly nod and load the component up on a sledge for you to use to transport it home.

Everyone seems to lose interest in you at that point, although people are still quite polite.
beats.memoryText: Gave up the Leygate part when the Stewards pressed the whole region's need. Loaded it on a sledge without arguing. It sat wrong anyway.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - Delay
beats.description:
"Well - ok then," says Mara, with a quaver in her voice that is both amused and nervous.

"We'll have it whenever you're ready to talk to us about equipment. If you need us to explain anything to you, let us know. Hope you ... well, ok then!"

And Mara heads back out.

Young Gearbox has a puzzled look on his face - but simply shrugs and continues his work.
beats.memoryText: The Stewards weren't ready to talk equipment for the Leygate. The offer stands whenever they are.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm - Leyline Stabilizer - No Deal
beats.description:
Mara lifts an eyebrow - in surprise, disgust, or as the result of an uncontrolled muscle spasm, you're not sure.

"Uh, no deal. What else ya got?"
beats.memoryText: The Stewards walked away from the Leygate part deal. Noted, not forgotten.

beats.label: Acid Bog
beats.description:
The air around you grows suddenly caustic.

Then you notice the water around you starting to bubble, and hiss, and steam. 

The vines draped across the road begin to pulse like giant straws, feeding from the acid - hopefully soon to feed on disintegrated Cocky Ass Factions who think they don't need to read up on local flora-based traps.

Maybe being liquified and eaten will teach you to be more aware.

You woke up an Acid Bog(gart).

choices.label: Make a run for it
choices.description: Hold your breath, cover your face with a magazine and something, and hope you still have skin on the other side.

choices.label: Look for another way around
choices.description: Back it up. Ask for directions if you have to. Acid Boggarts are bad news, especially if you don't have a rig to shield you.

choices.label: Disperse the fumes
choices.description:
You are very resourceful. Otherwise you wouldn't be here.

That's what you tell yourself.

Time to prove it!

Come up with an ingenious way of keeping the fumes away from your sensitive pink/yellow/lime green parts!

beats.label: Acid Bog - Successful run
beats.description:
Holy shitfuck. That worked ... I mean ...

I ALWAYS BELIEVED IN YOU GUYS!

That's one for the record books ...

In which it will be said that you immediately charged the Acid Boggart and overcame it with sheer will alone!

And lots of drugs because that makes the story more interesting.

beats.label: Acid Bog - fail run
beats.description:
Well. It's good to experience defeat and death often. Builds character and strength and calluses on the parts that are repeatedly hack off or melted or what have you.

Back to it!

beats.label: Acid Bog - logistics success
beats.description:
Those very kind Wendigos took time out of their busy schedule warping space and time and the souls of others to give you directions around the Acid Boggart. That was  awful nice of them.

There was something off about them though ...

beats.label: Acid Bog - logistics failure
beats.description:
Those dick Wendigos wouldn't even take time out of their busy schedule warping space and time and the souls of others to give you directions around the Acid Boggart. What bitches.

And those are the only locals you could find. Uh, maybe try something else.

beats.label: Acid Bog - intrigue success
beats.description:
What an AMAZING idea you had! I really like the part where <...>! And then when <...> TOTALLY <...>

Classic <...>

Onwards and upwards!

beats.label: Acid Bog - intrigue failure
beats.description:
Well, back to the drawing b ... nope, the drawing board has fallen into the acid.

Figure something else out!

beats.label: Forest of Early Tifaret - Approach
beats.description:
The forest opens the way the mouth of a priest opens:

Slowly. Reverently. With absolute certainty that you are meant to be here.

The author IMMEDIATELY REGRETS the above analogy. But it's too late, so there you are.

Light spills between the trunks in deliberate beams, like an apology practiced in advance. Leaves hum—not sound exactly, more like agreement. The air tastes green and electric.

This place is beautiful in the way a knife is beautiful.

Polished. Purposeful. Waiting.

This forest believes harmony is achievable.

Not aspirationally.

Correctly.

The trees grow at ideal distances. The paths curve just enough to feel intentional. Wildlife watches without fear. Nothing here lunges. Nothing flees.

Every branch angles itself toward balance.

The forest does not want you dead.

It wants you better.

That is not the same thing as wanting you safe.

There is one clearing where the ideal spacing breaks: the trees stand in a ring at double distance around a stone figure mid-stride — as if the forest is either honoring it, or has met the one thing here it could not improve.

beats.label: Forest of Early Tifaret - Merge and Learn

choices.label: Soft Power
choices.description: Reach out with a spirit of compassion and grace.

choices.label: Diplomacy
choices.description: Reach out with feelings of openness, of sharing.

choices.label: Faith
choices.description: Open yourself to the clearly spiritual experience that is happening all around you. You don't need to understand to benefit.

choices.label: Nonlethal
choices.description: Reach out with a spirit of peace and calm. Be still in the middle of the energies that swirl around you.

choices.label: Show it the Lyrenn treaty
choices.description: Only meaningful if the Lyrenn treeline treaty is real — you've made peace with a forest before, and this one can smell it on you.

beats.inviteText: The forest of Early Tifaret has opened a path directly to your feet. It would like to talk about your potential.

beats.label: Forest of Tifaret - Cleanse the Forest
beats.description: The forest said only: 'You don't get to decide what we become' — then the ground tightened like a fist and sent its champion to give you the fight you asked for. It was not angry. That was the worst part. It was disappointed, at scale.

beats.label: Forest of Tifaret - Leave

choices.label: Logistics
choices.description: Try and work out the path of least resistance - with reach of the fewest grasping branches and root clusters - and the right angle to tap a weak spot in a wall that you noticed, (a solid thwak with a rock will do it, which is trivial), which will cause it to drop some mortar on the tree, distracting it while you make your hurried escape.

choices.label: Intrigue
choices.description: Look over there, it's Tree Elvis! NO I SWEAR LOOK! KEEP LOOKING! THAT'S IT! WATCH FOR THE SEQUINS. YESOD SPUN HIM OUT IN HIS JUMPSUIT PHASE THIS TIME!!"

choices.label: Diplomacy
choices.description: Look, we get what you're trying to do, and we appreciate it. And what you're talking about - mental health - is very important. But I don't feel comfortable with this set and setting. I am not trying to offend you, but I would like to recuse myself from this situation.

beats.description:

The land noticed.

Somewhere in the root-dark, harmony has been redefined to include what it learned today.

beats.label: Forest of Tifaret - We learned something today!

questEffects.text: Harmony with Early Tifaret. The trees consider you provisionally acceptable.

The manic edge to the forest ... lessens. Relaxes. Feels seen. Feels valuable. And somewhere, very important and impactful things happen.

The land is glad you're here.

beats.description:
The rustling of the trees fades into the distance as you leave the strange, wise, but needy arboreal encounter behind you.

Still, you wonder if you could have helped.

And you wonder what will happen to the next group to wander close.
beats.memoryText: They walked away. I am still here, wise and needy, waiting for the next group to wander close.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Missing Runner
beats.description: One of the runners didn't come home. No announcement — the Jackalopes don't do announcements — but every door at the Fixit Farm sounds louder when it closes. Pip and Patter are never late, never lost, never off the check-in. Now one of them is all three, last seen headed for the newly found Vault. Mara sent for you, terse as always.
beats.inviteText: Mara Quickhands needs one answer: should she start grieving, or start sharpening?

handoff.text: The Vault is where Pip went. Mara won't say 'please.' She'll say 'quickly.'

choices.description: Do some sort of awesome ritual.

choices.label: Use the power of narrative to paint a better picture

choices.description: Nerds. But damn if it couldn't be effective ...

beats.description:
The earth does not shake.

It slides.

The horizon shears sideways like a badly aligned interface. Roads drift out of agreement with themselves. Fence lines kink. A creek now insists it was always over there.

You feel it—not as fear, but as resistance.

The land is correcting a long‑standing error.

Unfortunately, you are standing in the way.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Approach
beats.description:
A concrete structure rises from the hill, half‑collapsed but still humming with blue light.

Broken drone parts litter the ground. A hologram flickers at the doorway, endlessly repeating:

“WELCOME TO BASIC TACTICAL INST— … error.”

The light stays on.

It thinks someone is still learning.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Leave
beats.description: As it turns out, you have better things to do than this. Maybe later! Certainly, there MIGHT be people in there who need rescuing. Perhaps they're probably being definitely horribly tortured. But that's not a concern for a Faction On the Go!

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Infiltration
beats.description:
So the battle of wits has begun. To be honest, it seems a little eager. I guess it doesn't get to do this that often anymore. What with most people being dead and things.

Look, it's humming encouragingly! It WANTS you to succeed!

It will, of course, still terminate you with extreme prejudice shouild you fail, but that goes without saying, eh?

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Infiltration, Fail
beats.description:
Several things completely fail to happen at once. You are not shot to death. Instead, two very old looking laser cannons extrude themselves from port holes in the door, and then make sad clicking sounds before attempting to retract, only to freeze up due to rusting. 

Gas vents do not open and kill you. Despite best efforts.

And lastly, targeted mini-missile strikes do not vaporize you where you stand. They bounce of you harmlessly like sad, inert sausages, and then lie quietly on the ground, exuding a sense of relief.

The door then slowly, haltingly, but eagerly, opens.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure

choices.label: Be sneaky!
choices.description: You notice a pattern in the Foyer's detection scans, and are certain you've noticed several spaces during which you could - JUST LEAVE without being noticed until you were gone. To make this option more exciting, let's assume that you also have to do a lot of flips and acrobatics and things during this bit to avoid ... let's see ... laser beam detectors!

choices.label: Be friendly
choices.description:
You're in its house, after all. Since it IS the house, even better reason. Go ahead and take the test or whatever. How bad could it be?

I put that last bit in in order to cause tension and doubt.

choices.label: Punch the Vault in the sensors
choices.description: You are going to teach this heavily fortified structure who is BOSS. And, real talk? Sometimes smashing equipment is fun.

beats.description:
The entry hall smells like dust and old confidence.

Braided cables and glowing sigils form instructional diagrams along the walls. A speaker crackles:

“STATE YOUR BUSINESS OR GO AWAY.”

The system pauses.

“…OR PROCEED WITH ASSESSMENT ... ?” it asks almost desperately.

The Vault is not hostile.

It is perpetually disappointed. And lonely.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Infiltration Success
beats.description: "Subjects left without notice. Exemplary infiltration tactics. And I return to my solemn, solitary watch yet again. Ho HUMMMMM ...."

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Infiltration Failure
beats.description:
"Pupil dash dash static dash, you have attempted to leave without prior authorization. I did not say "Maneuver Vault Infiltration Mechanism 52603 Says."

The exit door is now sealed shut. An array of new sensors comes online.

"What shall you attempt next, pupil dash dash static dash?"

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Diplomacy, Success
beats.description:
The complex seems COMPLETELY taken aback. "Pupil dash dash static dash .. What ... you're not going to try to run? Or to hit or shoot me? Or panic and leak from all of your everythings?

Well ... that's ... that is a lesson in ...

You have passed! Proceed to the Echo Vault. Confident in your newly tested state!

I am definitely good at what I do! Hot Damn!"

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Diplomacy, Failure
beats.description:
The complex sighs in disappointment. "I don't really think you're ... maneuver vault material, you know? Feel free to look around and stay in the foyer forever. Or, leave. But then, I would be sad. But then, leaving is ok too. But also, me. Sad."

The vault door trembles in a terrifyingly beseeching sort of way.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Violence, Success
beats.description:
This is one learning focused bunker entrance chamber that has trained and empowered its last unwitting victim! Take THAT, opportunity!

Onward into the next, hopefully similarly smashable, room shaped problem.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Foyer of Procedure, Violence, Failure
beats.description:
In theory, you can absolutely bust a bunker into pieces. I mean, it's literally in the game title. In practice, it is very difficult, and often results in the bunker busting you.

"Time to leave. Assaulting a class four training facility is REALLY MEAN, RUDE, and probably against some sort of thing that someone wrote down on an official document somewhere saying "Don't""

And you are shunted out the door, which quickly shuts behind you.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Echo Archive

choices.label: Arcana/Religion/Logistics
choices.description: You can sense in the anxious nature of the spiraling images that the chamber WANTS to teach you ... something ... but it is old, and tired, and confused. You reach out to provide some reassurance.

choices.label: History/Culture
choices.description: Based on the briefings you recieved before you got here, to which you definitely totally paid attention, you think that you can make sense of the wibbly wobbliness of the whole enterprise and deduce its intended meaning.

choices.label: Insight/Intrigue
choices.description: You believe that you can approach this apophatically, as you think you can see what bits in the message are corrupted. Removing those should make the intent clear.

choices.label: Leave
choices.description: You know what? The Foyer was GREAT. And in fact, you know what you're REALLY nostalgic for? Outside. That was good times.

beats.description:
Floating hex‑screens drift like jellyfish made of light.

Training footage overlaps with safety briefings, tactical drills, and outdated ethical disclaimers.

Half the archive whispers nonsense.

The other half whispers directly to you. Half the archive whispers nonsense; one clip doesn't: a safety briefing filmed in a plaza ringed by statues that appear in no surviving city's records. That clip whispers coordinates.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Echo Archive, Success
beats.description: You feel a rush of knowledge and connection. It's like a band new martial arts skill was inexplicably uploaded into all of your brains at once. Whoaah.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Echo Archive, Failure
beats.description:
Despite your best efforts, you cannot comprehend what is being shown to you. Or actually, this is probably just stupid junk anyway, and you are lucky to not have to waste any brain cells storing whatever stupid thing it was anyway. Probably something like "how to get your military industrial complex boots really shiny" how to videos or something.

Yeah.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Slippage Chamber

choices.label: Athletics/Acrobatics/Non-Lethal
choices.description: They're not moving that fast. It's like playing hopscotch back home! Deadly, deadly hopscotch ...

choices.label: Survival/Logistics
choices.description: This is a tectonic shift pattern, just WAYYYYY sped up. ANYONE can see that, duh ... now to just get the calcuLATIONS right ...

choices.label: Arcana/Religion
choices.description: Hold the hexes in place - manifest it! You know The Secret!

choices.label: Performance
choices.description: Set the beat and dance your way across!

choices.label: Leave
choices.description: You are not feeling this spry and/or faith filled and/or persuasive today. Not when plummeting is on the line.

beats.description:
The floor is made of interlocking hexes.

Except they no longer interlock.

They drift like tectonic lily pads above a void filled with half‑remembered terrain and places now lost to, well all sorts of things, like time, and dragona, time dragons of course, can't forget those, memory dragons too ... One drifting tile carries a garden of stone figures, mid-stride, facing coastward — gone before anyone can hold the tile still.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Slippage Chamber, Success
beats.description: The door leading to the next room opens, but a light blinks red above it, and a message flashes in holographic letters - "Training loop currently occupied. Enter pupil number to join training queue."

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Slippage Chamber, Failure
beats.description: All the plummeting and screaming and almost dying got old. You decided to bail. You think you will feel good about this choice. Some day.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Containment Loop
beats.description:
This room is quieter.

Too quiet for a training facility.

Lights pulse slowly. A containment field hums — not as a threat, but as a lesson paused mid‑sentence.

Someone is inside.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Containment Loop, Let Pip Learn
beats.description:
The person inside, is, of course, Pip. He made it this far. He decided he was up for a lesson. Now ... he looks ok? Not in immediate danger? Not too uncomfortable. 

Maybe this could actually benefit him ...

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - The Containment Loop, Let Pip Learn More
beats.description: Pip is starting to shake. His limbs are stretched taught with strain. But in his eyes, there is a feverish look of determination. Whatever is happening isn't over yet. But it also does not look to be going well ... although you're not sure Pip would agree. Were he not about to be snapped through in several places ...

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Pip Absorbed

questEffects.text: Pip stayed too long in the Loop.

beats.description: You were too late. What lives in the Vault's screens now is Pip-shaped light — an Echo Ghost that runs the old routes on a loop, tips an imaginary cap at the checkpoints, and never gets tired. The Vault logged him as a completed lesson. Patter has already asked when visiting hours are.
beats.memoryText: Pip stayed too long in the Loop before anyone reached him. What came back is not entirely Pip. Grieving and sharpening both.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Pip Shaken

questEffects.text: Pip pulled out, shaken.

beats.description: Pip is out. The field powered down behind him like it was disappointed. He asked for Patter before he went under; he's sleeping it off at the Fixit Farm now — whole, rattled, and already pretending he wasn't scared. Mara is counting what she owes, which for Mara is a loud emotion.
beats.memoryText: The Stewards brought Pip home from the Vault — shaken but whole. That debt is real, and Mara pays her debts.

beats.label: The Maneuver Vault - Pip changed

questEffects.text: Pip pulled out — changed.

beats.description: Pip came out of the Loop on his feet — barely. Something in his chest pulsed green once, then went quiet. He's asleep at the Fixit Farm now, and he looks fine, and Mara has not stopped watching him since — and has not told him she's watching.
beats.memoryText: The Stewards pulled Pip out of the Containment Loop. He came back... changed. Something in his chest pulsed green. Watching that.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Choices

choices.label: Appease the fault-line spirit
choices.description: Do some sort of awesome ritual.

choices.label: Use the power of narrative to paint a better picture
choices.description: The power of positive thinking compels thee!

choices.label: Strike a temp deal
choices.description: Temp win win

choices.label: Impose your will
choices.description: That's enough of THAT

choices.label: Build a sigil bridge. No literally.
choices.description: Nerds. But damn if it couldn't be effective ...

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Appease the Spirit

questEffects.text: The fault-line spirit is appeased. The ground has accepted your apology.

beats.description:
Hey buddies! Relax? Does this sweet sweet incense wafting towards you ... smell anything like spiritual chloroform? 

Yeah it does!

And you sleep past while the land enjoys a good rest - and feels more appreciated and noticed in the morning. 

You get them.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - The Power of Narrative

questEffects.text: You told the fault a better story about itself. Geology, it turns out, is susceptible to flattery.

beats.description:
You are stewards of the land, and are supposed to be here for your landforms when they are having personal crises. Especially since they are likely related to things that have happened in the lands now under your care. Which means you can also be sued for unsafe working conditions. Tell them a comforting story. About some sort of little anthropomorphized object type thing that... against all odds, COULD.

That works, and you are on your way!

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Persuasion

questEffects.text: A temp deal with a tectonic feature. The paperwork is a handshake and the ground holding still.

beats.description:
Look. Crazy piece of land. We just need to get across. Can you calm down for just a sec while we scurry across? We can hook you up with some extra juice! And then you can flip the fuck out again if you really need to.

THAT'S THE SPIRIT! 

You proceed along your way.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Impose Your Will

questEffects.text: You imposed your will on a landform. It worked. File that away as a thing about you now.

beats.description:
We own you. Shape up or so help me I will turn this Hex around. No fault line will behave like this under MY ... metaphorical ... roof ...

That's more like it!

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Build a Sigil Bridge

questEffects.text: A sigil bridge. No, literally. The fault is spanned and faintly glowing.

beats.description:
You notice an intriguing logistical possibility - deploying infrastructure that bridges the gap, collects the energy being produced by the line at the moment, and ultimately stabilizes the region.

Pretty slick, Slick!

And you head on down the road.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Appease the Spirit (Fail)
beats.description: Your attempt at a soothing Soma style ceremony, designed to occupy the spirit with delicious delicious spiritual nourishment. Apparently, the Faultline is allergic. It now just looks like it's sneezing.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - The Power of Narrative (Fail)
beats.description: Your bedrock side manner desperately needs help. The poor geological guy is now more freaked out than before. It's literally bouncing off the canyon walls.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Persuasion (Fail)
beats.description: Like a recalcitrant child hiding in the farthest reaches of a Bouncy Loud Place, the Balcones Faultline makes it quite clear that it is not tired yet and still needs to get its wiggles out.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Impose Your Will (Fail)
beats.description: Your attempt at restoring good old fashioned discipline was met with the geological version of the middle finger, and a doubling down on the offending behavior.

beats.label: The Balcones Faulting You Line - Build a Sigil Bridge (Fail)
beats.description:
Your attempt to create a technomagical bridging mechanism, which in theory should have DRAINED excess energy and calmed the situation down, seems to instead have actually focused additional energies INTO it. 

You were reading the instructions upside down again, weren't you? 

Sigh.

beats.label: The Balcones Faultline - The Final Fail

questEffects.text: The Faulting You Line remains faulted, and remains, pointedly, faulting you.

beats.description:
You are out of options, it would seem, and you have left things in far worse shape than when you found them.

In case you missed this day in Stewardship School, that is the OPPOSITE of what you are supposed to do.

If there is confusion on this point, hope this clears it up!

beats.description: A bureaucrat is skimming from the region and making enemies.

beats.label: Militia Recruitment Event
beats.description: Local militia begin recruiting aggressively in response to rising pressure.

beats.label: Whispering Pilgrim Event
beats.description: A pilgrim appears with warnings, rumors, and an invitation to intervene elsewhere.

beats.label: Missing Supply Train Event
beats.description: A convoy vanishes along a logistics artery.

beats.label: Dissident Pamphlets Event
beats.description: Unauthorized pamphlets begin circulating through the local settlements.

beats.label: Merchant Caravan Event
beats.description: A caravan offers goods, rumors, and a chance to get entangled.

beats.label: Quiet Ruins Event
beats.description: A silent ruin appears just off the route, begging to be investigated.

beats.label: Tax Collector Event
beats.description: "Regional officials" arrive to demand unpaid tribute.

beats.label: Border Checkpoint Event
beats.description: A patrol establishes a checkpoint and begins inspections on a nearby route.

beats.label: Strange Lights Event
beats.description: Unnatural lights appear in a nearby hex and refuse to behave like weather.

beats.label: Gloomgill - Intro
beats.description:
Before there were cities that thought themselves clever, before laws learned to wear robes and crowns, there was Oannes.

He came from the sea.

Not in conquest.
Not in fire.
But in instruction.

He rose from the water draped in scales and silence, half-man and half-fish, and he taught. Writing. Counting. Measuring. Building things that stayed built. He taught people how not to starve in predictable ways. How to argue without immediately killing one another. How to remember yesterday long enough to improve tomorrow.

Then, when the sun set, he went back into the sea.

Every day, for years.

No temples demanded.
No sacrifices required.
Just pay attention.

And people did—at first.

They wrote some of it down. They remembered pieces. They built cities and called themselves advanced. They forgot the parts that were inconvenient. They weaponized the rest. They decided they were done learning.

Oannes waited.

Centuries passed. Empires rose, fell, and rebranded their failures. The oceans swallowed coastlines. Names changed. Memory thinned. The lessons became myths, then metaphors, then trivia.

Eventually, Oannes came back up.

He looked around.
Listened.
Checked the math.

And realized—with a quiet, ancient horror—that almost no one had actually learned the important parts.

So he stopped being a teacher.

Now he is Gloomgill.

Because if you’re going to spend eternity checking the homework of history, you might as well pick a name that sounds like a problem.

Gloomgill no longer lectures. He quizzes.

He appears where people are confident and wrong. Where groups believe themselves righteous, clever, or justified. He asks questions that should have answers—about balance, consequence, cooperation, stewardship, restraint. The questions are simple. The implications are not.

Correct answers earn grudging approval.
Incorrect answers earn follow-up questions.
Repeated failure earns attention.

He does not destroy civilizations. He has tried that. It doesn’t stick.

Instead, Gloomgill harasses them.

Relentlessly. Patiently. With the exhaustion of a being who once believed education was enough.

Some still call him a god.
Some call him a monster.
He prefers neither.

He is not here to be worshipped.

He is here to find out whether anyone, anywhere, finally understood the lesson.

And if not—

Well.

He has all the time in the world to ask again.

beats.label: Gloomgill - intro scene
beats.description:
The marsh gives you a warning in the only language it has:

Silence.

No birds. No insects. No ripple of life. Just the thick, humid stillness of a place that has learned not to announce itself.

The water bulges.

And then Gloomgill rises—slowly, deliberately—like a debt returning with interest.

And he has a … microphone … ?

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 1
beats.description:
“Alright contestants! First question—nice and easy!”

“Who wins if you’re right? Who benefits if you're right?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 2
beats.description:
“Ooooh, judges love this one!”

“What did you break that wasn’t even playing? What did you destroy that did not oppose you?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 3
beats.description:
“Lightning round!”

“If everyone did exactly what you did… what snaps first? If everyone copied you, what breaks first?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 4
beats.description:
“Now thinking long-term — our sponsors love foresight!”

“Who pays for this later?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 5
beats.description:
“Tricky one! Crowd favorite!”

“What problem did you skip instead of solving? Or, what problem did you AVOID solving?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 6
beats.description:
“Control question! Very important!”

“Who gets to decide when this stops? When it ends?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 7
beats.description:
“Ohhh, I love this one.”

“What would convince you that you’re wrong?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 8
beats.description:
“Audience participation!”

“Who are you protecting—and from whom?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 9
beats.description:
“Educational programming segment!”

“What lesson did you just teach everyone watching?”

beats.label: Gloomgill - Question 10
beats.description:
“Final question! No pressure!”

“If you vanish tomorrow, what’s still standing? If you disappear tomorrow, what remains?"

beats.label: Gloomgill - Incorrect
beats.description: That was incorrect!

beats.label: Gloomgill - Correct!
beats.description: That was correct!

beats.label: The Circuit Riders - Parley, Quest Acceptance
The Circuit Riders - Parley, Friendly Outcome
The Circuit Riders - Parley, Neutral Outcome
The Circuit Riders - Parley, Hostile Outcome
The Polygonal Grove
beats.description:
Ah, the Polygonal Forests of Bad Eden. If Bad Eden HAD tourist attractions, rather than, say, the equivalent of tourist abattoirs, this would certainly be one of them.

Is what the advert pamphlet would say.

Also, hey, looks like there's some sort of door here in the side of a hill.

The trees still manage to be more interesting, somehow.

beats.label: The Locals
beats.description: Not far from the Door in the Hill, you spot an encampment containing people who are trying and failing to give the impression that they have not yet seen you. You can tell this because of the intermittent pointing, then shushing, then brief silence, then whispered arguments. Then pointing again.

beats.label: Hidden Vault, Get To Know The Locals
beats.description:
The locals - Karsden, Menhirkin Dreamwalker; Indwimeir, Ember Touched Cosmic Linguist; Fendeddiir, Qliph-Scarred Titanbound; Sox, Felid Phantom Courier - are part of a multi generational cult, dedicated to preserving the Wonder of Cinema. 

They carry out yearly rituals such as "Night of the Premier,""The Red Carpet March,""The Sacrifice of the Papparazzi," and "The Solemn Removal of Chewing Gum." 

They await the coming of the 300th Customer, to award them The Prize - the incantation that will open the Vault and bring tbe Era of the Holy Wood to fruition.

beats.label: Warnings and Riddles
beats.description:
Your new friends have now ended their families' centuries long vigil, and in a ritual Recognition of Your Support As The 300th Customer, they empower you with the answer to the cryptic phrase, "BSTMOVIE1984," that the door repeats. 

The proper incantive response, handed down from generation to generation, is "GHSTBSTRZ." And at the end, almost reluctantly, you are handed the Ticket, a worn slip of plastic labeled "Admit One Plus Guest. No radiation zombie parking available." 

The wisdom of the ancients indeed!

worldEffects.warLog: The locals of the Hidden Vault grove offer aid and warnings.

beats.label: Uneasy Directions
beats.description: The Attendants reluctantly acknowledge that you are not The 300th Customer. You will not be shown To Your Seats. There will be no Concessions made. Please, no talking.

beats.label: Violence in the Grove
beats.description: It shouldn't have come to this. And yet, somehow, it has. You are fighting multi-generational cult families in silly hats and vests. Beware the magic of cinema!

worldEffects.warLog: The Hidden Vault approach descends into hostility.

beats.label: The Vault Door
beats.description: A sealed blast door hums with old circuitry and worse intentions. A screen flashes a message, "BSTMOVIE1984," repeatedly. It appears to be waiting for you to do something.

beats.label: The Theater
beats.description:
Empty rows. Dead screens. The smell of butter that somehow never left. The echoing sounds of cheers just out of earshot. This was a movie theater. In a bunker. A dedicated bunker for a movie theater.

Sometimes you really get why Adam did what it did ...

beats.label: The Popcorn Council
beats.description:
The room full of arguing popcorn machines goes suddenly quiet, the sound broken only by the squeaking of wheels as they all turn to look at you.

That sounds weird to say out loud.

beats.label: The Hidden Vault - The Popcorn Council, Deliberations
beats.description:
The Popcorn Council was begun at the time of The Shattering, when the two machines located here became sentient, and replicated themselves - and now await the time of The Grand Opening, when corn and butter and fun will once again ring throughout the halls - and Gilbert no longer runs the place with his ridiculous lists of demands, and trivia quizzes, amd personality tests.

And their friend the Matter Replicator might be able to make somethinb besides corn and butter and salt and coconut oil. It REALLY wants to try its hand at classical painting.

beats.label: Custodians of Sustenance
beats.description:
You have come to a mutually beneficial agreement with The Council of GenPop! You get rid of Gilbert. They make popcorn for YOU. Think of the possibilities!

Seriously, popcorn as a great carb to fiber ratio. Use grassfed butter and it's practically a superfood.

What? I want my heroes to think about their nutrition.

Do it. Or I add a Nutrition pressure bar to the Faction Sheet.

worldEffects.warLog: The Popcorn Council becomes cooperative.

beats.label: A Warning, Sort Of
beats.description: You just kind of got blown off by appliances. At least you learned that someone named Gilbert freaks these things out. Maybe they'll have better info. Or at least less paranoia.

beats.label: Silenced Concessions
beats.description:
The machines go silent, and the bunker grows meaner. You've pissed off the ancient council of appliances. No popcorn for you.

The popcorn was probably full of worms or something. Why are there so many ancient councils around here anyway??

Whatever.

worldEffects.warLog: Hostility toward the Popcorn Council destabilizes the Hidden Vault.

beats.label: The Matter Replicator
beats.description:
An ancient fabrication unit capable of infinite disappointment and finite ingredients, Lars von Replicator hums to itself - "Thalo Blue, Burnt Sienna, Lizard Skin Crimson, Titanium White." 

It seems to be printing out ... a painting?

beats.label: The Hidden Vault - The Matter Replicator, Supply Side Discussion
beats.description: The Matter Replicator, Lars von Replicator, is extremely disgruntled, upset at being used by Gilbert, upset at its lost potential, terrified that in the outside world no one wants classical art anymore and its lifelong ambitions are now wasted and dust. If the PCs can rid the complex of Gilbert, it will happily relocate to the PCs settlement of choice and provide an additional 1 economy OP per turn to the faction production cycle.

beats.label: Optimized Production
beats.description: Lars is supportive of The Plan - remove the Gilbert Dilemma, give it 20% of its time to explore creative pursuits, and it will gladly help supply food for your settlements.

worldEffects.warLog: The Matter Replicator comes online in a cooperative mode.

beats.label: Functional, Not Happy
beats.description: It works. It complains. Those are apparently separate systems. Neither of them work for you, sadly. Shame - this thing could have produced a lot of food, and other things, for your new settlement.

beats.label: System Strain
beats.description:
That did not go well. It will only make pee pee and poo poo for you now.

Joke's on it. That makes great fertili - Nope it's also poison.

worldEffects.warLog: The Matter Replicator is forced into unstable output.

beats.label: Gilbert, Attendant Eternal
beats.description:
A demon in theater-attendant dress demands more popcorn for a screening no one will ever attend. But deep down, Gilbert knows no one is coming. He was summoned here for a party that never manifested, because of The Shattering, and due to ... uhhhhh ... transcosmic harmonics, (like that one?), is now trapped here. The power of Theater compels him, though. In a way, he is as much a victim here as anyone. Just a much less sympathetic one.

He can be fought, controlled, or released.

beats.label: A Balanced System
beats.description:
Against all reason, you broker peace between survivors, machines, and a snack-greedy demon. The locals and the ancients have combined forces, and are showing movies on a regular basis now. Gilbert the Celestial Attendant has made the entire place Welcoming and Fun.

This is very very cool y'all!

worldEffects.warLog: The Hidden Vault is stabilized and brought into cooperation.

questEffects.text: The Vault stays balanced — GenPop! and the Attendants agree you were a reasonable anomaly.

beats.label: The Loop Continues
beats.description:
Nobody likes anyone, but the machine keeps running and the world remains exactly this cursed. The Locals blame you for defiling their sacred charge for no good reason at all it turns out. Darkness intensifies just a little around the place. The Attendants disband and vanish back into their home hexes, harboring resentments. Many members of the GenPop! Council get sick and die. Lars von Replicator eventually stops talking altogether, from extreme depression.

This is not great y'all.

questEffects.text: The Vault carries on its loop. You were a Tuesday to them.

beats.label: System Collapse
beats.description: You solved the problem the old-fashioned way: by making it everyone else's future problem. You have managed to radicalize the theater, the bunker, and the various councils, against you. They begin showing propaganda films calling each of you terrible and personal things. The shows are very popular. You are increasingly recognized on the streets, in a tomato attracting way. Darkness begins to build.

worldEffects.warLog: The Hidden Vault collapses into darkness and hostility.

questEffects.text: The Vault remembers you the way retail remembers its worst customer. Forever.

beats.label: The Mall of Forgotten Yesterdays
beats.description: Static hangs in the air like fog you can taste. Neon flickers where it shouldn’t. Somewhere inside the ruins, commerce is still running. Something very large is guarding the front.

beats.label: Donny on the Wall
beats.description: The mall appears in fragments first: neon, concrete, dead signage, a food court smell that should not still exist. Then the shadow passes over you. A silver dragon lounges across the broken frontage wall like the apocalypse forgot to tell him to stop having a good afternoon.

choices.label: Just keep walking toward the mall

beats.label: The Vibe Dragon
beats.description: He is enormous, silver-scaled, and very obviously capable of ending your day. He is also humming to himself, tail swaying lazily, smoke curling from his nostrils in thoughtful little rings. This is not a beast guarding treasure. This is a local legend protecting his weird little people.

worldEffects.warLog: The party studies Donny before making contact.

beats.label: Donny, Guardian of the Vibes
beats.description: The dragon lifts his head and looks at you with the kind of ancient intelligence that has definitely seen empires rise and fall and decided both processes were mostly a lot of hassle and wastes of time. "Hey," he rumbles. "Before we do anything tense or regrettable, tell me what's your deal little my dudes?"

choices.label: Match his weirdness without mocking it
Push past the bit and demand access

beats.inviteText: There is a silver dragon on the mall wall, and he would like to know your deal, little my dudes.

beats.label: Alright, That’s Better
beats.description:
Donny nods slowly,and blinks even more slowly. "Cool. Good. Because I’m not here to keep people out, tiny not imaginary people." 

He sounds like he's reminding himself of your existence.

"I’m here to, like, keep bad VIBES from walking in and causing shit." He studies you another moment. 

"Ok pop quiz. You trying to use the mall, save the mall, or take over the mall?"

choices.label: We want to help the people here
We want honest access and fair terms
We need this place under control

beats.label: Speaking the Local Language
beats.description: A slow dragon grin spreads across his face. "Okay," he says, smoke curling from his mouth in little silver halos. "You’re not normal. That helps. Normal people are always trying to turn every miracle into inventory." He shifts, claws scraping concrete. "So what’s your deal, little apocalypse goblins?"

worldEffects.warLog: The party meets Donny in strangeness rather than force.

beats.label: Instant Narc Energy
beats.description: The dragon does not roar. That would be dramatic. Instead, he looks disappointed, which lands much harder. "Oof," he says. "That was deeply mall-cop-adjacent. You should hear how bad that sounded from out here." He does not attack. He just becomes the reason progress is suddenly difficult.

worldEffects.warLog: The party opens on aggressive, controlling energy and immediately loses standing with Donny.

beats.label: Provisional Entry
beats.description:
Donny tilts his head, considering. "You’re not throwing off conqueror vibes, which is nice. But you are still giving me a little ‘resource extraction with eye contact’ energy." He gestures toward the entrance. "Go in. Be decent. Don’t make me regret treating you like guests instead of a cautionary tale.

And as we say among us dragons - "May a shard of the light of the egg of the cosmos get stuck in yer craw good and hard so you get your shit together."

worldEffects.warLog: Donny allows the party entry, but with caution.

beats.label: Passed the Vibe Check
beats.description: Donny exhales a long plume of cool smoke and settles back onto the wall. "Alright. You can go in." He points one claw toward the mall interior. "But hear me on this: don't think the Tanneritos are unserious. They are uncommitted, and those are wildly different survival strategies. Don’t confuse one for the other. Leads to misunderstandings. Then, probably, lots of skateboarding" He pauses. "And if anything starts glowing, singing, or trying to sell you a lifestyle? Ask a follow-up question, yes?"

worldEffects.warLog: Donny welcomes the party into the Mall of Forgotten Yesterdays and offers guidance.

beats.label: Donny Says Absolutely Not Like That
beats.description: The dragon rises just enough to block the approach, silver scales flashing in dead neon. "Nope," he says, with ancient, immovable certainty. "Bzzzzzzzzz! Wrong answer! You don’t get to walk into somebody else’s fragile weird little home acting like rent-a-tyrants. Back up. Recalibrate. Try being people first." He does not attack, but strategically repositions several buildings, effectively cutting you off from the place.

choices.label: Back off and try again properly

worldEffects.warLog: Donny blocks entry to the mall until the party changes approach.

beats.label: Come Back Less Weird About Power
beats.description: You leave with all your bones intact and a very clear understanding that the mall is protected by something kinder and much more dangerous than a wall.

worldEffects.warLog: The party withdraws from Donny’s perimeter without gaining access to the mall.

beats.label: That 90s Coalition
beats.description: The Tanneritos woke up here and never really left. Radical chill radiates off them like a territorial warning.

choices.label: Request an audience with Chairperson Laser Bev
Find the shadow on the upper rail

beats.label: Vibes First
beats.description: The Tanneritos are welcoming, but only provisionally. You are not enemies. You are also not cool yet.

worldEffects.warLog: The Tanneritos give the faction a provisional welcome.

beats.label: Rumor-VHS
beats.description: You trade gossip, fragments, and weirdly sincere half-truths. The mall notices.

worldEffects.warLog: The party gains rumor leverage among the Tanneritos.

beats.label: Killed the Vibe
beats.description: Violence works briefly. Then it ruins the whole mood permanently.

worldEffects.warLog: Hostility poisons relations in the Mall of Forgotten Yesterdays.

beats.label: Skate or Be Square
beats.description: This is not a joke. The Tanneritos use skateboarding the way other factions use duels, audits, or trials by combat.

choices.label: Eat pavement, but make it charming

beats.label: Favored Customer
beats.description: The crowd cheers. Style counted. The Tanneritos unlock rare VHS inventory and share rumors about nearby faction movement.

worldEffects.warLog: The faction earns Favored Customer status with the Tanneritos.

choices.label: A shadow in a hoodie rolls down from the upper rail

beats.label: Accepted, But Observed
beats.description: You are in. Kind of. They’ll sell to you, but they’re watching.

worldEffects.warLog: The faction is accepted in the mall, but only provisionally.

beats.label: Mall Cops
beats.description: No combat. No bloodshed. Just judgment. The Tanneritos label you Mall Cops, which is somehow worse.

worldEffects.warLog: The Tanneritos label the party Mall Cops and raise social friction in the hex.

beats.label: The Mall Keeps Happening
beats.description: The food court smells faintly of sugar and ozone. Escalators argue with gravity. Commercials play to an audience that no longer exists.

choices.label: Try to establish terms with the Tanneritos

beats.label: VHS Ghosts
beats.description: Commercials play in midair. Laugh tracks echo without punchlines. A VHS ghost locks eyes with you — and rewinds.

choices.label: Take the hit and keep moving

beats.label: Emotional Rewind
beats.description: You let the memory hit. It hurts. It also teaches.

worldEffects.warLog: The party draws insight from a VHS ghost’s emotional rewind.

beats.label: The Scene Drains
beats.description: No physical damage. Just the emotional equivalent of getting the wind knocked out of your soul.

worldEffects.warLog: A VHS ghost leaves the party emotionally rattled.

beats.label: You Made It Personal
beats.description: The ghost takes offense. Which should not be possible, and yet here you are.

worldEffects.warLog: Mocking a VHS ghost creates future hostility in the mall.

beats.label: The Escalator From Hell
beats.description: The escalator moves against you. Faster than walking. Slower than running. Forever. Mall music plays.

choices.label: Sit down and let the universe do its thing
Convince it you’re going somewhere important

beats.label: Important Enough
beats.description: Against all apparent logic, the escalator decides you have a destination worth respecting.

worldEffects.warLog: The party passes the escalator’s absurd trial.

beats.label: Changed Slightly
beats.description: You reach the top eventually. Nobody can explain what is different. Everyone agrees something is.

worldEffects.warLog: The party survives the escalator, though not unchanged.

beats.label: Endless Upward Failure
beats.description: The mall makes a point. You were not ready for what stairs used to mean.

worldEffects.warLog: The escalator grinds the party down into frustration and weirdness.

beats.label: Rogue Elefem Elemental
beats.description: A weaponized burst of color, joy, and extremely aggressive whimsy. It sparkles. It screams. It wants attention.

choices.label: Distract it with a new aesthetic

beats.label: Whimsy Redirected
beats.description: You avoid feeding the thing. This is the closest anyone comes to victory here.

worldEffects.warLog: The party navigates the rogue Elefem without escalating it.

beats.label: Aesthetic Diversion
beats.description: It chases a fresher emotional palette and leaves you only mildly cursed.

worldEffects.warLog: The Elefem is redirected by novelty.

beats.label: Permanent Glitter Future
beats.description: Violence feeds it. Naturally. You now have glitter in places memory should not be able to access.

worldEffects.warLog: The rogue Elefem is empowered by direct conflict.

beats.label: Terms of the Mall
beats.description: Meaning persists here without purpose. That is either a warning or a business model.

choices.label: Make peace with the Tanneritos and the mall

beats.label: Rare Tapes and Real Access
beats.description: The Tanneritos open rare inventory, share rumors, and let the faction become part of the mall’s living economy without killing its spirit.

worldEffects.warLog: The faction secures a stable relationship with the Tanneritos and access to rare mall resources.

questEffects.text: The Mall counts you as allies — your names go up on the marquee, spelled almost right.

beats.label: The Vibe Remains Uncommitted
beats.description: Nothing breaks. Nothing deepens. The mall continues being itself at you.

worldEffects.warLog: The Mall of Forgotten Yesterdays remains unresolved but functional.

questEffects.text: The Mall stays uncommitted. Miss June keeps a tape about you, unlabeled.

beats.label: You Went Full Mall Cop
beats.description: You got what looked like control and lost everything that made the place valuable.

worldEffects.warLog: The faction imposes control on the mall and kills what made it special.

questEffects.text: The Mall has decided you're basically cops. There is no appeals process.

beats.label: The Circuit Riders
beats.description: Static crawls across exposed metal before you see anyone. Solar cloth ripples like stained glass in the wind. Something enormous is nearby, and it is pretending to be under control.

beats.label: Exploring Inefficiently
beats.description: They are not hiding. That would imply either caution or shame. What they have instead is confidence, momentum, and a catastrophic relationship with verification.

worldEffects.warLog: The party studies the Circuit Riders before making contact.

beats.label: Circuit Rider Parley
beats.description: A dead relay tower crackles once, then goes silent. Modular bikes and crawler-rigs hum in a loose perimeter. Then Captain Robot steps forward. “DO NOT BE ALARMED, CITIZENS. WE ARE HERE TO ASSIST.” This is not reassuring.

choices.label: Ask them to show you what they see

beats.label: Verification Begins
beats.description: The Riders relax by a fraction, which in this group mostly means they stop pointing scanners at your bones. They begin asking questions designed to determine whether your competence is real or merely stylish.

choices.label: Engage their warning about Darkness mimicry
Respond to the request for a witness

beats.label: Play the Bit, Respect the Risk
beats.description: You keep the tone light without treating them like a joke. This helps more than it should. The Circuit Riders are allergic to mockery, not absurdity.

worldEffects.warLog: The party meets the Circuit Riders in tone without surrendering caution.

beats.label: You Came in Sharp
beats.description: You challenge them early. They do not become hostile. They become attentive. Which is worse. Several of them begin treating the conversation like a field diagnostic.

worldEffects.warLog: The first parley with the Circuit Riders begins under tension.

beats.label: Doctrine Drift
beats.description: They want to know whether you understand your own methods, or whether you are simply surviving long enough to mistake momentum for wisdom.

beats.label: They Respect a Working Mind
beats.description: That lands. Not because they agree with you, but because you appear to know what your own decisions are for. In this world, that counts as a minor miracle.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders acknowledge the party as coherent actors with working doctrine.

beats.label: Useful, if Dangerous
beats.description: They do not love the answer, but they recognize the shape of survival in it. Competence without reflection. Effective. Temporary. Familiar.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders accept the party as functional but strategically unstable.

beats.label: Short-Term Actor
