beats.description: That answer earns silence. Not offended silence. Calculating silence. They have seen enough collapsing systems to recognize one wearing a face.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders mark the party as strategically shallow.

beats.label: Darkness Mimicry
beats.description: They warn that Darkness has learned to imitate optimization. Faster loops. Cleaner logic. Less hesitation. All the right shapes, none of the right reasons.

beats.label: Shared Threat Model
beats.description: That gets their attention. Not agreement. Alignment. The difference matters, and they know you know it.

worldEffects.warLog: The party and Circuit Riders align around the threat of Darkness mimicry.

beats.label: Concern Registered
beats.description: They accept the answer. Not warmly. But enough to keep the channel open.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders keep the party under cautious observation.

beats.label: You Missed the Point
beats.description: The room temperature changes. One of the Riders notes something on a handheld slate. You suspect it is about you.

worldEffects.warLog: The party dismisses the Riders' warning and is marked as a concern.

beats.label: Witness Request
beats.description: They want someone to see what they see and survive it. Not because they need permission. Because they need confirmation that reality is still shared.

beats.label: Witness Accepted
beats.description: That matters more than it should. You have not promised obedience. You have promised to look. For them, that is almost sacred.

worldEffects.warLog: The party accepts a witness role in future Circuit Rider operations.

beats.label: Deferred, Not Denied
beats.description: They let that stand. For now. Not trust. Not disappointment. Just an open file with your name on it.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders leave the witness request unresolved.

beats.label: Refusal Logged
beats.description: The answer is accepted with the kind of calm that suggests it has already become a future category.

worldEffects.warLog: The party refuses the Circuit Riders' request and is marked accordingly.

beats.label: Terms of Contact
beats.description: Captain Robot stands perfectly still while the rest of the Riders subtly evaluate whether you are useful, dangerous, or both. Somewhere beyond the tents, something enormous shifts its weight.

beats.label: Shared Intel, Future Support
beats.description: No great oath. No swelling music. Just a mutual recognition that the future is going to get weirder, and it may be strategically useful not to face it alone. Captain Robot does not promise sentiment. He promises response. If the call comes clean, and if trust has been earned, the Circuit Riders will come hard, fast, and without theatrical delay.

worldEffects.warLog: The party secures a meaningful alliance with Captain Robot and the Circuit Riders, with the possibility of future intervention support.

questEffects.text: The Riders ride with you — when the call comes clean, they come.

beats.label: Surveillance, Not Hostility
beats.description: You are not allies. You are not enemies. You are, however, now on a list maintained by people who think firmware is a moral category.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders maintain ongoing surveillance without open hostility.

questEffects.text: The Riders neither friend nor flag you. Out here, that's a compliment.

beats.label: Short-Term Actors
beats.description: They decide you are the kind of people who may survive the next problem while becoming the one after that. No violence. No alliance. Just classification.

worldEffects.warLog: The Circuit Riders flag the party as short-term actors requiring caution.

questEffects.text: Flagged by the Circuit Riders. Their network is faster than your apology.
Flagged by the Circuit Riders. Their network is faster than your apology.

beats.label: The Sky Breaks Sideways
beats.description: They do not hide the bunker. They orbit it. Ships drift in lazy spirals above a cracked bunker mouth carved into the bones of the world. Engines scream. Someone is singing badly. Inside: a Yesodic Spark. Inside: answers. Inside: people who will absolutely make this harder than it needs to be.

beats.label: Alarm Is a Language
beats.description: You slip past rope-lines that hum like they remember hands. Inside, the bunker is alive with motion, laughter, and terrible decisions. Then you touch the wrong knot. The entire place inhales. Alarm spreads like gossip. You are now part of the story.

beats.label: The Spark, Unwitnessed
beats.description: You take it. The Yesodic Spark hums like a memory trying to become real again. You also take something else: records. Monodynamic Industries. They did not mean to hurt Khezek Tor. They redirected the energy using the seal and sent the impact somewhere farther up the line. You can feel the wound from here.

worldEffects.warLog: The party infiltrates the Valhaulan bunker, steals the Yesodic Spark, and uncovers partial Monodynamic records tied to the injury of Khezek Tor.

beats.label: Caught in the Middle of Someone Else's Party
beats.description: They do not get angry. They get excited. You are no longer intruders. You are now entertainment.

worldEffects.warLog: The party's infiltration attempt collapses into open exposure inside the Valhaulan bunker.

beats.label: Sklar Bjrornholt, Unfortunately Impressed
beats.description: She grins when she sees you. “That’s bold. Walking in like that. I like you already.” She offers a drink. You should not take it. You will probably take it anyway. Sklar is charismatic, perceptive, and absolutely capable of turning negotiation into a weather event.

choices.label: Be direct about the Spark and Monodynamic
Match her tone and earn respect

beats.label: A Dangerous Kind of Respect
beats.description: You tell the truth cleanly enough that she believes you are either brave or terminally sincere. Both earn points. She admits the Valhaulans were acting on Monodynamic direction. They used the seal to redirect energies from Khezek Tor, but they did not know what they were striking. They know now that the place was injured, not merely tapped.

worldEffects.warLog: The party earns Sklar Bjrornholt's respect and learns the Valhaulans were covertly used by Monodynamic Industries in the redirection of Khezek Tor's energies.

beats.label: Friends, For Now
beats.description: She laughs hard enough to nearly start a secondary incident. “Fine. Take the Spark. We don't even know what it does. But the people who pointed us at that job? They knew enough to lie by omission.” She spits the Monodynamic name like it owes her money.

worldEffects.warLog: The party wins over Sklar Bjrornholt, acquires the Yesodic Spark, and receives strong Monodynamic intel under unexpectedly friendly terms.

beats.label: Not Enemies. Not Friends.
beats.description: She shrugs. “Well. Worth a shot.” You are allowed to leave, which is somehow more humiliating than being thrown out. You do not get the Spark. You do not get the good intel. You do get a very clear sense that this could have gone better.

worldEffects.warLog: The party fails to secure terms with Sklar and leaves the Valhaulan bunker without the Spark.

beats.label: Violence, Enthusiastically
beats.description: They cheer when you attack. This is the best day some of them have had all month. The bunker erupts into motion: ropes, engines, blade-light, bad singing, and very committed tactical stupidity. If the Circuit Riders are with you, the field gets much louder and significantly more correct.

choices.label: Press the assault and break their momentum
Lose the tempo and get bogged down

beats.label: Victory, With Applause
beats.description: You win hard enough that even they have to respect it. Some of them literally do. You secure the bunker interior, seize the Spark, and strip the place for records before anyone has fully processed whose side they were on fifteen minutes ago.

worldEffects.warLog: The party takes the Valhaulan bunker by assault, secures the Yesodic Spark, and recovers operational intel tied to Monodynamic Industries.

beats.label: Momentum Is a Lie
beats.description: You hit hard. They hit harder. Or stranger. Or just longer. The bunker holds. The sky refuses to become yours. You are forced back without the Spark, and the Valhaulans now have a much clearer opinion of you.

worldEffects.warLog: The assault on the Valhaulan bunker fails, hardening hostilities and denying the party access to the Spark.

beats.label: The Long Way Around
beats.description: You lock it down. Starve the routes. Cut the angles. Wait for the bunker to become smaller than its own appetite. If the Circuit Riders assist, the perimeter becomes cleaner, more oppressive, and much harder to break. The Valhaulans do not crack quickly. They adapt, joke, improvise, and become a problem in shifts.

beats.label: They Open the Doors Themselves
beats.description: Eventually Sklar leans out from the bunker mouth and yells, “Okay, this has stopped being fun.” Terms are made. The Spark is yielded. The intel comes in fragments, but enough of the pattern is visible now: Monodynamic pointed them at a sealed energetic redirection they did not understand, and Khezek Tor paid the price.

worldEffects.warLog: The siege succeeds. The Valhaulans concede the Yesodic Spark and provide partial intel linking Monodynamic to Khezek Tor's injury.

beats.label: You Cannot Starve a Storm
beats.description: The perimeter frays. Someone gets clever. Then several someones get louder than clever. The bunker does not break before your line does. You withdraw with losses, frustration, and no Spark to show for it.

worldEffects.warLog: The siege collapses before the Valhaulans do, leaving the bunker unconquered and the Spark out of reach.

beats.label: Unexpectedly Friendly Terms
beats.description: You are not family. Let us not get irresponsible. But you are no longer strangers and no longer targets. The Valhaulans deal with you as people worth calling back. In Bad Eden, that is dangerously close to friendship.

worldEffects.warLog: The Valhaulans and the party part on unexpectedly friendly terms.

questEffects.text: The Valhaulans deal with you as people worth calling back.

beats.label: Clean Exit, Dirty Truth
beats.description: You got what you came for. Not elegantly. Not gloriously. But successfully enough that history will round in your favor. The Spark is yours. The truth is incomplete, but it points in the right direction: Monodynamic redirected energies through the seal and wounded something ancient in the process.

worldEffects.warLog: The party escapes with the Yesodic Spark and partial Monodynamic intel, but without securing warm relations with the Valhaulans.

questEffects.text: Clean exit, dirty truth — the Spark secured.

beats.label: Not Today
beats.description: You leave without the Spark. No alliance. No war. Just a closed door and the knowledge that Bad Eden does not care whether you were close.

worldEffects.warLog: The party fails to obtain the Yesodic Spark and leaves the Valhaulan bunker on neutral but unproductive terms.

questEffects.text: Not today. The arc closes; the sky remembers.

beats.label: You Will See Them Again
beats.description: You leave without the Spark, and now they know your shape. The Valhaulans will remember this. So will the people behind them. Nothing is resolved. It has merely become personal.

worldEffects.warLog: The raid on the Valhaulan bunker ends in failure and hostility, ensuring future conflict.

questEffects.text: You will see them again.

beats.label: Sky-Forged Gifts
beats.description: They give you things they absolutely should not. Because they like you. Because they are bored. Because this will be funny later. You leave with the Yesodic Spark, strong Monodynamic intel, and a handful of very dangerous expressions of trust.

worldEffects.warLog: The party receives major Valhaulan rewards, including gear, maneuvers, and strategic support options.

questEffects.text: Thatward's Ho! The long line ends where the lying stops. Major spoils.

beats.label: Spoils of the Sideways War
beats.description: Whether through force or hard leverage, you come away with the Spark and enough plunder to matter. Not friendship. Not exactly. But respect leaves useful wreckage.

worldEffects.warLog: The party secures standard rewards from the Valhaulan bunker, including the Yesodic Spark and battlefield spoils.

questEffects.text: Thatward's Ho! Done, dusted, and divvied.

beats.label: The Spark and the Scar
beats.description: You got the Yesodic Spark and enough intelligence to know the shape of the crime, even if not every hand behind it. Monodynamic used the Valhaulans as deniable vectors. Khezek Tor was not merely tapped. It was injured. That matters.

worldEffects.warLog: The party secures the Yesodic Spark and partial strategic intelligence regarding Monodynamic and Khezek Tor.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Gilbert Appears

choices.label: Try to calm him down
choices.description: This is diplomacy, emergency facilities management, and customer service exorcism all at once.

choices.label: Square up
choices.description: Well. The usher has chosen violence. Or panic chose it for him.

encounter.actorName: Gilbert, Eternally Cleaning Not Leaning Theater Attendant

beats.description: The old theater still has its marquee, though half the bulbs have gone mad and the other half have become critics. One sputtering line remains legible: GHOSTBUSTERS - ONE NIGHT ONLY. Inside, the carpet is sticky with thirty years of deferred tragedy. The popcorn machine is shouting at the soda fountain about standards. From somewhere in the dark, a frantic voice snaps: "NO, no, no, no, the guests are early, the floors are appalling, the projector is emotionally compromised, and absolutely no one is READY!" Then Gilbert rounds the corner in a storm of mop water, ticket stubs, and incandescent professional despair.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Fight Gilbert

choices.label: If he breaks, try to reach him
choices.description: Because sometimes the boss fight is actually against a cosmic panic attack with a broom.

encounter.actorName: Gilbert, Eternally Cleaning Not Leaning Theater Attendant

worldEffects.warLog: Gilbert erupts into a frenzy of impossible cleanliness, trying to purge the theater of all imperfection before the guests arrive.

beats.description: Gilbert attacks with the full authority of a man who has been failed by appliances, patrons, and history. Seat backs snap upright. Mop water arcs like a curse. Somewhere, a film reel screams.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Talk Gilbert Down

choices.label: Help him get the theater ready
choices.description: Clean, sort, reassure, delegate, and treat the coming audience like a promise instead of a threat.

choices.label: Appeal to culture and civic joy
choices.description: Tell him the point of a theater is people together in the dark for the right reasons, not perfect floors.

choices.label: Perform the opening ritual properly
choices.description: Ticket. Lights. Curtain. Welcome. You are not fighting a monster now; you are onboarding an institution.

choices.label: Remind him he is not alone
choices.description: The guests are not a judgment. They are a community waiting to be invited back in.

beats.description: Gilbert is spiraling. But spirals can invert. Under the panic there is duty. Under the duty there is care. Under the care there is a beautiful, exhausted idiot who just wanted opening night to matter.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Gilbert Spirals Harder
beats.description: "NOT READY," Gilbert cries, now on the verge of metaphysical collapse. "You keep saying helpful things in the tone of people who have never had a soda line revolt on opening night!" A mop bucket overturns itself in solidarity.

beats.label: The Bad Eden Bijou - Assistant Manager of Light
beats.tags: theme.auditor resolved culture faith economy sephirotic

worldEffects.warLog: Gilbert's panic inverts into purpose. The old theater reopens as a public house of story, ritual, and concessions. The Bijou now produces Culture and Faith through gathering, and Economy through food, tickets, and side hustle snack theology.

questEffects.text: The Gilbert matter is settled, theatrically. The Vault resumes its programming.

beats.description: Something in Gilbert straightens that has been bent since the Shattering. The broom lowers. The lights warm. The arguing appliances become merely opinionated. Gilbert smooths his vest, inhales like the first calm breath of his existence, and says, with trembling dignity: "Right. Of course. We do not prepare for guests because we fear them. We prepare because welcome is sacred." The theater opens. The projector steadies. Popcorn becomes a civic instrument. Gilbert, now a Sephirotic Assistant Manager, begins programming repertory nights, matinees, educational screenings, and deeply sincere concession bundles.

beats.label: Chairperson Laser Bev
beats.description: The office used to be a sunglasses kiosk. It still kind of is. Acrylic shelves gleam under dead neon. Behind the counter sits a woman in a faded windbreaker, mirrored shades pushed up into her hair, annotating a legal pad with a glitter pen that radiates executive menace. She looks up once. “So. You got past Donny, nobody died, and the mall still feels like itself. Strong start. I’m Chairperson Laser Bev. Yes, it’s an elected title. Yes, that is funny. No, that does not make it less binding.”

choices.label: How are you in charge of this place?
What do the Tanneritos actually want?
What would make us useful to you?
What do you think of Donny?
Do you have an echo story?
Can we establish terms with the Tanneritos?

beats.inviteText: Chairperson Laser Bev will see you now. Bring your own sunglasses; the kiosk stopped selling them before the world ended.

beats.label: Laser Bev — Why She’s in Charge
beats.description: Laser Bev smiles like she’s heard this from people who later regretted asking. “Same way anybody’s in charge of anything worth having. I solve the problem that keeps coming back. Leaks. Feuds. tape disputes. heartbreak. concession routing. ghost inventory drift. Also two separate incidents involving cursed Orange Juliuses. I’m in charge because when weird little systems start to wobble, I can hear which screw is lying.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — What the Tanneritos Want
beats.description: “Continuity without calcification.” She lets that sit there. “We want the mall to remain weird, inhabited, and ours. We want trade without annexation. We want traffic without conquest. We want enough safety that people can be soft here without somebody mistaking that for weakness. And if possible, we’d also like to stop finding raccoon bones in the old Sbarro.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — Permanence is Suspicious
beats.description: “Permanence is how bad ideas put on a necktie. Every empire that came through here wanted to call itself inevitable. Every one of them said the same thing in a different font.” Her tone sharpens. “We prefer renewable consent.” Then, lighter: “It also helps with decor.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — What Makes You Useful
beats.description: She studies you carefully. “Finish what you start. Don’t confuse being invited with being trusted. Don’t ‘stabilize’ us into somebody else’s comfort. And if one of your people buys a memory-tape, make damn sure they know the difference between curiosity and looting.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — On Donny
beats.description: Laser Bev’s whole face softens by about four percent. “Donny is a sweetheart with tactical apocalypse boundaries. If he lets somebody through, it means he believes they might still choose decency. Don’t make him feel stupid. He takes that personally in a very draconic register.”

beats.label: Laser Bev — Terms
beats.description: “Terms are easy. You don’t get to own us because you map us. You don’t get to govern us because you survive us. Trade is possible. Alliance is possible. Mutual aid is possible. Acquisition is not.”

worldEffects.warLog: The party establishes preliminary non-acquisition terms with Chairperson Laser Bev.

beats.label: Laser Bev — Echo
beats.description: Laser Bev goes still. “I used to believe structure was enough. I made a place orderly once. Efficient. Predictable. Nobody ever had to wonder what the rules were.” Her mouth tightens. “That place could not survive grief.” A long pause. “I think I’m here to build something that bends before it breaks. And to make sure irony never again becomes an excuse for not loving people on purpose.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus
beats.description: You notice him only after you’ve already been watched by him for a while. A shape peels off the railings and halfpipe shadows: too thin in one angle, too many elbows in another, hoodie full of static, board tucked under one arm like a ritual implement. His wheels do not quite touch the ground. He lands without impact. The air around him smells like dust, cherry soda, scraped palms, and impossible second chances. He nods once. “Hey. You ate shit interestingly.”

choices.label: Why is skating such a big deal here?
What makes somebody a mall cop?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Historically, Plural
beats.description: He considers this. “Historically? Plural. You get enough kids trying to become themselves in the same square footage, eventually the floor remembers the shape of it. I’m what happens when commitment leaves a groove.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Why Skating Matters
beats.description: He looks offended by how obvious the answer is. “Because it tells the truth. You can fake diplomacy. You can fake confidence. You can fake theology for, like, a shockingly long time. You cannot fake a landing. And if you eat pavement, you also can’t fake what you do next.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — What Style Is
beats.description: Kickflip Lazarus laughs. “Style is not elegance. Style is not difficulty. Style is not looking expensive. Style is whether your body and your choice arrive in the same place at the same time. Style is honesty at speed.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Mall Cops
beats.description: He answers instantly. “Trying to control a place before you’ve let it change you. Thinking access is the same as permission. Thinking a map is the same as a relationship. Using the word ‘asset’ with your whole chest.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Can He Teach You?
beats.description: He grins. “Absolutely. Badly, at first. The lesson is not ‘be good.’ The lesson is ‘stop negotiating with embarrassment.’”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Run It Back
beats.description: Kickflip Lazarus rolls alongside the PC who wiped out hardest. “Okay,” he says. “Now do one more. No crowd this time. No clout. No proving. Just you and the thing you were trying not to feel the first time.”

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Locally Real
beats.description: Kickflip Lazarus watches the finish and nods once. “There you go. Locally real.” It is not a title. It is better than one.

worldEffects.warLog: Kickflip Lazarus acknowledges the party as locally real within the mall.

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Still Hiding
beats.description: He nods, not unkindly. “Cool. You’re still hiding.” No punishment. Just a truth that hangs around.

worldEffects.warLog: Kickflip Lazarus notes that the party is still hiding from itself.

beats.label: Kickflip Lazarus — Echo
beats.description: Kickflip Lazarus stares at the food court skylight. “There was a night where somebody had to go first. Nobody knew the trick. Nobody knew if the rail would hold. Everybody wanted somebody else to become the story. I think I’m what remained of the kid who decided embarrassment was cheaper than regret. And I’ve been teaching that lesson ever since.”

beats.label: Miss June of the Endcap
beats.description: The fluorescent lights buzz with impossible retail determination. Shelves of tapes line the walls in perfect, obsessive rows: action, romance, apology, weather, unsent arguments, one whole section labeled SUMMER THAT BIT YOU A LITTLE. Behind the counter stands a woman in a store vest from three hundred years ago, translucent at the edges and immaculate in bearing. Her nametag reads: JUNE. She smiles like she has explained the return policy to the dead. “Welcome to the Exchange. Please do not remove any memories from their original sleeves unless you are prepared to own the fingerprints.”

choices.label: What exactly do you sell here?
How does the VHS exchange work?
What do the Tanneritos get out of this?
Do the VHS ghosts work for you?
Show us what’s in rare inventory.
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Miss June — What She Sells
beats.description: “Mostly context. Sometimes that looks like tapes. Sometimes that looks like rumors. Sometimes that looks like the exact commercial jingle necessary to make a ghost remember its own name. And occasionally, for premium members, closure.”

beats.label: Miss June — How the Exchange Works
beats.description: “Fairly,” she says, which is somehow more threatening than reassuring. “You may buy with favors, stories, uncommon sincerity, or tradable knowledge. Cash is accepted only if it has a history interesting enough to justify the insult. Rare inventory opens to those who have demonstrated either kindness or taste. Ideally both. We are not animals.”

beats.label: Miss June — Rumor-VHS
beats.description: “Compressed social weather. Some rumors are just information. Others are experiences wearing information as a hat. A rumor-VHS lets you feel the shape of what people are not saying plainly.” A beat. “Side effects may include borrowed certainty, misplaced nostalgia, and the temporary conviction that you absolutely used to know a girl named Amanda.”

beats.label: Miss June — What the Tanneritos Get
beats.description: Miss June’s smile gets smaller, sharper. “Continuity. You call it commerce because that makes it sound optional. I call it circulation because otherwise the mall begins to clot. Places die when nothing meaningful moves through them.”

beats.label: Miss June — On VHS Ghosts
beats.description: “Oh, good heavens, no. They collaborate, occasionally. They haunt freelance. Treat them gently and they become archivists. Mock them and they become editors.”

beats.label: Miss June — Rare Inventory
beats.description: Miss June slides several tapes onto the counter without quite letting go of them. “How To Survive The First Version of Yourself. Directors’ Cut: Somebody Else’s Bad Decision. Mallwalker Summer Preview Reel. Employee Training Video: De-Escalation, Smiling, and Fire.” Her smile remains professionally serene. “Rare inventory, as always, requires reciprocal sincerity.”

worldEffects.warLog: Miss June reveals rare inventory at the VHS Exchange.

beats.label: Miss June — Echo
beats.description: Miss June goes very still. “I used to believe that if I could just place everything correctly, nobody would panic. Right shelf. Right label. Right tone. Right smile. Right substitution when the thing they wanted was gone.” A pause. “Then one day the world ran out of equivalents.” Her gaze flicks over the tapes. “I think I’m here because memory still deserves handling instructions. And because people are gentler, sometimes, when desire has to be named before it can be met.”

beats.label: Captain Robot
beats.description: Captain Robot steps forward with the precise, measured gait of a man who learned dignity inside a machine and never misplaced it after. The suit is patched, old, and lovingly maintained; not a disguise, not a joke, not armor exactly, but a decision that never stopped being useful. His voice comes through a grill that should make him sound absurd. It does not. “Verification first,” he says. “Friendship second. Rescue third. If you skip the order, people die in the wrong sequence.”

choices.label: Why are you called Captain Robot?
What do the Circuit Riders actually want?
What do you mean by verification?
Would you ever come to someone’s aid in a real fight?
What would make you trust us?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Captain Robot — Why the Name Stayed
beats.description: He tilts his head, servo whine soft and almost embarrassed. “Because people started saying it as a joke, and then too many frightened people relaxed when they heard it. A ridiculous name that lowers pulse rate is tactically valuable. Also,” a beat, “I have earned it.”

beats.label: Captain Robot — What the Riders Want
beats.description: “A future that can survive contact with reality.” He gestures toward the rigs, the relay tower, the watchful perimeter. “We do not need purity. We do not need ideology polished to a mirror finish. We need patterns that remain themselves under stress. We move. We verify. We intervene where drift becomes lethal. Good folks, mostly. But good folks who have buried enough optimists to become procedural.”

beats.label: Captain Robot — Verification
beats.description: “Verification means we do not trust a beautiful theory until it survives dirty conditions.” He folds his hands behind his back. “Darkness has learned to imitate efficiency. Bad doctrine now arrives looking optimized. If your decisions get faster, colder, cleaner, and you never once ask what got left out, then congratulations: you may already be obeying something that hates you.”

beats.label: Captain Robot — Rescue
beats.description: Captain Robot goes still in a way that makes everyone else around him also become more still. “Yes,” he says. “If alliance is real, and if the call is clean, and if we can verify that arriving will save lives rather than merely decorate a disaster, then yes. We come hard. We come fast. We do not come theatrically.” A beat. “Earn that sentence, and it may matter later.”

worldEffects.warLog: Captain Robot confirms the Circuit Riders may intervene in a future crisis if trust is earned.

beats.label: Captain Robot — Trust
beats.description: “Three things,” he says. “Admit uncertainty before it costs someone else. Finish an intervention after the interesting part is over. And when you are shown a pattern that implicates you, do not get romantic about your intentions.” The helmet turns a fraction. “Intentions are weather. Follow-through is architecture.”

beats.label: Captain Robot — Echo
beats.description: For a while, only the wind speaks against the solar cloth. Then: “There was an evacuation once,” he says. “I had the numbers. I had the route. I had the confidence of a man who had mistaken prediction for care.” His gauntleted hand tightens once. “I moved the correct number of people to the wrong kind of safety.” A long pause. “I think I am here to keep competence from becoming cruelty with good posture.”

beats.label: Simone
beats.description: Simone has the still, unnerving calm of somebody who can hear a machine fail before it knows it is dying. She does not look at your weapons first. She looks at your timing. “Captain Robot checks whether you mean well,” she says. “I check whether you lag.”

choices.label: What do you mean by lag?
How would we help your people?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Simone — Lag
beats.description: “The gap between recognizing a truth and acting like you recognized it.” She says this as if it should embarrass civilization. “Some people call that hesitation. Some call it diplomacy. Some call it leadership. I call it where casualties breed.”

beats.label: Simone — How to Help
beats.description: She points toward a relay rack with half its casing removed. “When something starts failing, do not assign a committee to admire the fracture. Stabilize. Then discuss. Your faction feels capable. I am trying to determine whether it is also interruptible.”

beats.label: Simone — Echo
beats.description: Simone’s expression does not change much. “I once had enough warning to save everyone,” she says. “So I used it to optimize the outcome.” She finally looks straight at you. “That sentence has blood in it.” A pause. “I think I’m here to intervene before the elegant answer arrives.”

beats.label: Arvind
beats.description: Arvind is surrounded by disassembled signal gear and the mild aura of a man who has sworn at invisible math until it apologized. He offers a brief nod. “I handle communication, interpretation, and the ongoing tragedy of people hearing patterns they like more than the ones that are there.”

choices.label: Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Arvind — Patterns
beats.description: “Decision loops. Repetition signatures. The shape of justification after an ugly choice.” He adjusts a cracked lens. “Bad systems repeat differently than wounded people do. The trouble is that both can sound persuasive if you are tired.”

beats.label: Arvind — Darkness and Optimization
beats.description: “By offering cleaner choices than reality permits.” He says it with professional contempt. “No residue. No ambiguity. No grief accounting. Just throughput.” His mouth twists. “Anything that promises human decisions without human cost is either selling, lying, or hungry.”

beats.label: Arvind — Echo
beats.description: Arvind exhales slowly. “I once ignored a distortion because it validated the larger model.” He taps the side of the relay dish beside him. “It was beautiful. Coherent. Wrong.” A beat. “People died inside my confidence interval. I’m here because interpretation should hurt more when it risks becoming vanity.”

beats.label: Howard
beats.description: Howard has the broad, patient look of someone who could carry an engine block, a wounded scout, or a bad conversation to safety without complaining. He gives you the sort of nod that means he’s willing to like you later if you don’t make a project of disappointing him now.

choices.label: What do you do for the Riders?
What would alliance actually mean to you?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Howard — What He Does
beats.description: “Recovery,” he says. “People, machines, signal towers, plans that turned out to have opinions.” He shrugs. “Mostly I go get what someone clever left in the wrong place too long.”

beats.label: Howard — Alliance
beats.description: Howard thinks before answering. “It means when one of us says ‘this is going bad fast,’ the other side does not ask for a presentation deck.” A beat. “It means your emergency is allowed to become mine without first becoming a transaction.”

worldEffects.warLog: Howard frames alliance with the Circuit Riders as practical mutual aid under pressure.

beats.label: Howard — Echo
beats.description: He rubs the back of his neck. “I left somebody once because I was following the plan.” The sentence lands like dropped metal. “The plan was efficient. I was efficient. He still died alone.” Howard looks past you toward the rigs. “I’m here so the right thing can interrupt the prepared thing before it’s too late.”

beats.label: Dennis
beats.description: Dennis has the bright-eyed look of a person who finds three new problems per hour and is somehow delighted by all of them. He is halfway inside a crawler-rig panel and talks to you from there. “I’m Dennis. If Captain Robot is the caution and Howard is the follow-through, I am the regrettable but occasionally necessary hypothesis.”

choices.label: That feels ominous. What do you do?
Would you really show up in a rescue?
Do you have an echo story?

beats.label: Dennis — Hypothesis
beats.description: Dennis grins from inside the machine. “I test edge cases before they become funerals. Fast routes. weird fixes. stupid ideas with excellent time-to-impact. Somebody has to ask whether the impossible option is merely underfunded.”

beats.label: Dennis — Rescue
beats.description: He pops back out of the panel, unexpectedly serious. “Yeah. Absolutely. Good folks are worth moving fast for. But speed without verification is just panic with branding. So if we come, we come because someone here did the work of becoming believable.”

beats.label: Dennis — Echo
beats.description: Dennis looks away first. “I had a theory once that should have stayed a draft.” He laughs once, without humor. “Turns out ‘probably fine’ is not a load-bearing phrase.” A pause. “I think I’m here so ingenuity has to answer to aftermath before it gets promoted to culture.”

beats.label: Witness Request
beats.description: Captain Robot signals, and the Riders stop talking long enough for the camp itself to become legible. Relay drift. predictive overlays. route revisions. casualty maps with three futures each. “We will show you,” he says. “But not for free. You do not get to witness our burden casually.”

choices.label: Stay with the human cost of it
Acknowledge what this knowledge costs them

beats.label: You Stayed For the Whole Pattern
beats.description: The data stops looking abstract. That is the test. Captain Robot studies your face and gives a small, almost invisible nod. “Good,” he says. “You did not reduce us to a capability. That improves your odds.”

worldEffects.warLog: The party witnesses the Circuit Riders' burden without reducing it to abstraction.

beats.label: You Saw the Pattern, Not the People
beats.description: The projections blur back into symbols before you can hold onto what mattered. No one mocks you. That makes it worse. Arvind quietly powers down one of the displays. Captain Robot says, “Come back when your need to understand is less hungry.”

worldEffects.warLog: The party fails to fully grasp what the Circuit Riders are asking them to witness.

beats.label: The Rotating Chapel

choices.label: Enter carefully and map the rotations
choices.description: Treat the place like evidence, not shelter.

choices.label: Force the mechanism and expose what moves
choices.description: Break concealment by breaking elegance.

choices.label: Consecrate or harmonize the space first
choices.description: Ask the chapel what it remembers before you interrogate it.

beats.description: The chapel looks abandoned right up until it subtly isn't. Its steeple shifts a few degrees when no one is looking directly at it. The pews all face different directions. The place feels less haunted than calibrated. Somebody has been using this sanctuary as a compass for guilt.

beats.label: The Chapel Turns Toward Intent

choices.label: Take the coastal routing clue and move on
choices.description: The notes point toward a scorched coastal discharge site.

worldEffects.warLog: The party maps the Rotating Chapel and uncovers evidence of repeated directional seal testing tied to the coast.

questEffects.text: The chapel's alignments sketched.

beats.description: You hold position, mark angles, and wait. The interior rotates in tiny devotional corrections whenever attention drifts. It is not random. The alignments correspond to repeated seal orientations — a sequence of deliberate re-aiming, not one desperate mistake. Someone practiced redirection here.

beats.label: You Learn More, Worse

choices.label: Pocket the fragment and head for the Burnt Flats

worldEffects.warLog: The party forces the Rotating Chapel and recovers directional hardware, but leaves the place spiritually offended.

questEffects.text: The chapel forced; a bearing recovered.

beats.description: The hidden locking assembly gives way with a shriek like a hymn being corrected by violence. You recover a stripped directional ring and a coded destination fragment, but the whole structure shudders in disapproval. The chapel was hiding a workflow. It did not appreciate being audited with a crowbar.

beats.label: A Safer Kind of Listening

worldEffects.warLog: The party harmonizes the Rotating Chapel and confirms the existence of a coastward three-point redirection pattern.

questEffects.text: The chapel witnessed; the bearing held.

beats.description: When treated as a witness instead of a machine, the chapel settles. The rotations slow. One final alignment holds long enough to sketch cleanly: coastward, through a three-point chain. You leave with less hard evidence, but more trust in the pattern. Sometimes reverence is just better forensics.

beats.label: The Burnt Flats

choices.label: Read the residue as a pattern, not damage
choices.description: Work out what happened here and what did not.

choices.label: Excavate the fused marker rod from the mud
choices.description: Pull the clue out of the scar by hand.

choices.label: Leave before the Flats decide to answer back

questEffects.text: The trail moved on to the Burnt Flats.

beats.description: The Burnt Flats should be cold ash and bad memory. Instead, the mud still exhales heat in geometric seams. Pools flash with iridescent skin where no oil should be, and blackened reeds bend against the wind to point inland. This was not a wildfire. This was a receipt.

beats.label: The Scar Was Skipped, Not Struck

choices.label: Follow the harmonic corruption into the Mire

worldEffects.warLog: The party determines the Burnt Flats were a pass-through discharge scar in a larger redirection chain.

questEffects.text: The discharge pattern read.

beats.description: That’s the ugly truth: the Flats were not the destination. They were brushed aside by something routed with intent. This site bears proof of passage, not impact. Whatever the seal was doing, it was moving burden through this place toward somewhere worse. Or more useful.

beats.label: Still a Clue, Still Gross

choices.label: Press on toward the Singing Mire

worldEffects.warLog: The party gathers partial evidence at the Burnt Flats and confirms a directional anomaly linked to the coast.

questEffects.text: A partial read of the flats.

beats.description: You do not get the whole truth, but you get enough to be worried professionally. The heat lines are directional. The site was involved, not accidental. And whatever went through here kept going.

beats.label: The Singing Mire

choices.label: Tell the truth and listen
choices.description: Let the place tune around honesty.

choices.label: Counter-harmonize and push back
choices.description: Meet the song with structure of your own.

choices.label: Shut it down and keep moving
choices.description: A terrible but efficient instinct.

questEffects.text: The trail moved on to the Singing Mire.

beats.description: The mire sings before you see it. Not birdsong. Not wind. Harmony. Human-adjacent, wrong-throated, accusatory harmony. Each of you hears a slightly different line. The mud brightens when someone avoids a hard truth. The reeds tremble when anyone starts deciding who ought to bear the cost.

beats.label: The Mire Rewards Honesty, Which Is Rude

worldEffects.warLog: The party earns the Singing Mire’s clearest clue: the pattern points toward Anchor Reach.

questEffects.text: The mire's harmonic answered true.

beats.description: The harmony resolves when nobody lies. Not into safety — into legibility. A repeated phrase emerges through the rot-song: Anchor Reach. Not a destination exactly. More like the place the pattern expects to be believed.

beats.label: You Answer the Song

worldEffects.warLog: The party counter-harmonizes the Singing Mire and confirms Anchor Reach as the closing point in the coastal pattern.

questEffects.text: The mire countered; the note still carried.

beats.description: You force structure onto the wrong harmony and, to your surprise, it answers like an insulted choir director. The pattern clarifies just enough to show a triangle closing on Anchor Reach. You have not made friends with the swamp. You have, however, gotten cited by it.

beats.label: The Swamp Judges Your Tone

worldEffects.warLog: The party survives the Singing Mire and confirms the corruption is harmonic rather than random.

questEffects.text: A partial read of the mire.

beats.description: You get through, but not gracefully. The song curdles into static behind you. Even so, one thing is undeniable now: the corruption here is tuned. Someone built this problem to resonate.

beats.label: Anchor Reach

choices.label: Stabilize the pattern long enough to study it
Break an anchor point and stop further routing
Mark the site and follow the human logistics trail

questEffects.text: The trail moved on to Anchor Reach.

beats.description: At low tide the harbor floor becomes a diagram. Anchor chains, drowned pilings, and snapped moorings form a shape that does not look accidental once you’ve seen the other two sites. This is not where the burden began. This is where it was made to hold still long enough to be redirected. At low tide, the diagram shows its pilings. One of the drowned pilings has shoulders.

beats.label: Now the Pattern Makes Sense

worldEffects.warLog: The party stabilizes Anchor Reach and fully reconstructs the three-point coastal redirection pattern, implicating Port Kudzu.

questEffects.text: The anchor stabilized; the triangle closed.

beats.description: The whole triangle snaps into legibility. Burnt Flats was the pass-through scar. Singing Mire was the harmonic saturator. Anchor Reach was the fixative. The redirection needed a logistics node to monetize or move the outcome. Port Kudzu is no longer a rumor. It is the next page in the same crime.
beats.memoryText: They held the pattern still long enough to read it. The harborfolk say the Stewards study before they smash — around here, that's a reputation.

beats.label: You Break the Diagram Before It Breaks You

choices.label: Find the people who were using it

worldEffects.warLog: The party breaks Anchor Reach’s pattern-anchor, stopping future routing but destroying some of the best evidence.

questEffects.text: The anchor broken; the triangle closed anyway.

beats.description: The chain gives with a scream of salt and rust. The pattern collapses before it can be used again, but not before one ugly surge rips through the shallows. You stop the machine. You also erase some of the cleanest proof. Very frontier. Very mixed blessing.
beats.memoryText: They smashed an anchor point, and the proof went down with it. The surge was ugly. The harborfolk noticed who caused it.

beats.label: Port Kudzu

choices.label: Win a broker over with respect and patience
Steal a manifest and let morality catch up later

questEffects.text: The heading carried to Port Kudzu.

beats.description: Port Kudzu floats on denial, rope, and invoices nobody wants associated with their name. Every dock has three stories and at least one of them is true enough to ruin somebody. The captains here do not hide information. They rent it by the breath.

beats.label: The Captain Who Saw the Water Go Sideways

choices.label: Take the evidence to Legansus Waystation
Cross-check it with the Crown Mall archive

worldEffects.warLog: At Port Kudzu, the party confirms the coastal discharge chain was organized and supported by human logistics.

questEffects.text: Harbor testimony gathered.

beats.description: The story comes out in pieces, because truth this expensive is rarely served whole. A river captain saw the surge move inland against expectation, then split according to a route somebody clearly prepared in advance. The paperwork links back to chapel-marked cargo and inland handling codes. Congratulations. It was organized.

beats.label: Bad Harbor, Still Useful

choices.label: Seek outside validation at Legansus Waystation

worldEffects.warLog: The party leaves Port Kudzu with partial but actionable evidence of an organized inland-coastal routing scheme.

questEffects.text: Partial testimony gathered.

beats.description: You do not get a clean confession, but you do get enough to be dangerous: route codes, a chapel reference, and confirmation that someone inland expected a redirected event to pay off. Kudzu remains a bad place to underestimate and a worse place to bluff.

beats.label: Legansus Waystation

choices.label: Submit to verification and show your evidence
Hold some things back and test them first

questEffects.text: The trail moved on to Legansus Waystation.

beats.description: The waystation is half relay tower, half civic sermon about maintenance. The Circuit Riders here have the look of people who already know the shape of the problem and are deciding whether you are useful, dangerous, or merely loud enough to accelerate it.

beats.label: Verified Actors

worldEffects.warLog: Legansus Waystation verifies the party’s evidence and confirms a broader infrastructure anomaly consistent with redirected burden.

questEffects.text: The waystation verified the manifests.

beats.description: The Riders do not praise you. That would be weird and emotionally irresponsible. They do, however, confirm that your evidence tracks with wider machine anomalies and that somebody has indeed been trying to turn infrastructure debt into a regional weapon. They advise corroboration before confrontation.

beats.label: Useful, But Watched

choices.label: Go get corroboration at Crown Mall

worldEffects.warLog: Legansus Waystation provisionally validates the party’s findings but flags them as incomplete actors pending corroboration.

questEffects.text: The waystation flagged the manifests.

beats.description: The Riders do not reject you. They classify you. That somehow feels ruder. They confirm enough to keep you moving, but make it very clear that incomplete honesty around this kind of pressure gets people archived in the wrong category.

beats.label: Crown Mall Archive Access

choices.label: Approach respectfully and ask for corroboration
Treat the archive like a state asset and see what happens
choices.description: A bold and terrible instinct.

questEffects.text: The trail reached the Crown Mall.
The trail reached the Crown Mall.

beats.description: Crown Mall is what happens when a ruin decides retail was a valid metaphysics after all. The Tanneritos do not preserve history in the official sense. They preserve route memory, social residue, old footage, dead ads, and enough vibes to convict a government. Which is close enough.
beats.inviteText: The Tanneritos say the mall remembers lights over the coast — for the right kind of visitor.

beats.label: The Food Court of Corroboration

choices.label: Done. This cluster is now real and dangerous.
choices.description: You have what you need to build the next layer of campaign consequences.

worldEffects.warLog: At Crown Mall, the party corroborates the chapel-coast-port routing scheme with archived route memory and old commercial records.

questEffects.text: The archives corroborate: the bunker is real.

beats.description: The archive coughs up exactly the kind of evidence only a mall could preserve: dead shipping promos, route boards, kiosk invoices, and a camcorder clip of lights moving wrong over the coast before anyone publicly admitted anything was happening. It is absurd. It is definitive. You now have corroboration from the least respectable respectable source on the frontier. Among the camcorder clips, a dead advertisement plays on loop: 'Visit the Founders' Garden — one hundred figures in living stone' — with a route board showing the way. Nobody at the mall knows if the exit still exists.
beats.memoryText: The archive helped them; the mall is on the record. The Tanneritos filed the whole visit under 'polite, paid, welcome back.'

beats.label: You Are Being Kind of a Cop About This

choices.label: Leave with what you managed to salvage

worldEffects.warLog: The party fumbles archive diplomacy at Crown Mall and leaves with partial corroboration but weakened standing.

questEffects.text: Enough corroboration: the bunker is real.

beats.description: The Tanneritos do not fully refuse you. They do, however, become dramatically less helpful. You still learn that old route media exists and that somebody in the mall remembers lights over the coast. But you leave with less access and a strong social note attached to your file in whatever impossible way this place keeps files.
beats.memoryText: They came in acting like the law. The archive answered like a mall: technically open, spiritually closed. There is a note in their file now.

beats.label: Lost Stone Statue - Northreach Expanse b

choices.label: Stand your ground in silence
choices.description: Endure the pressure without reaching for spectacle.

choices.label: Challenge the statue directly
choices.description: If it wants proof, give it conflict.

beats.description: The first statue rises from a shallow basin in the open plains, half-submerged and facing a horizon that no longer deserves that level of confidence. Its face is weathered away. Its posture is not. One hand is open. One is clenched. Heat rolls off the stone when anyone boasts. The Spark of Geburah here is not asleep. It is waiting to see whether strength arrives as discipline or appetite.

beats.label: Geburah Fragment I - Measured Strength

worldEffects.warLog: At Northreach Expanse b, the party earns the first Geburah fragment through restraint rather than brute force.

beats.description: The statue's open hand fills with ember-light. It does not reward fury. It rewards restraint under pressure. The first fragment of Geburah tears free like a coal refusing to die. Somewhere in the distance, something old and martial decides you may not be a joke after all.

beats.label: Geburah Fragment I - Taken the Hard Way

worldEffects.warLog: At Northreach Expanse b, the party seizes the first Geburah fragment by force.

beats.description: The basin erupts in violent red light and the statue answers with motion that should have remained impossible. You win, or at least survive the argument, and wrench the fragment free. It comes hot, sharp, and resentful. A valid frontier solution. Also the kind that leaves a mark.

beats.label: Lost Stone Statue - Inconvenient Mountains.q

choices.label: Climb, bleed, and do not complain
choices.description: Demonstrate endurance without theatre.

choices.label: Break the basin and take what you came for
choices.description: A loud, terrible, efficient plan.

beats.description: The second statue is wedged into a mountain pool high above the road, one knee bent, chin lowered, blade across its lap. Wind needles the skin. The climb up here is its own insult. This fragment of Geburah seems less interested in whether you can win and more interested in whether you can continue when continuing is stupid.

beats.label: Geburah Fragment II - Endurance

worldEffects.warLog: At Inconvenient Mountains.q, the party earns the second Geburah fragment through endurance.

beats.description: The blade hums. The storm stills. A shard of disciplined red radiance rises from the statue's chest and settles into your keeping. This one was never about winning quickly. It was about refusing collapse when collapse had a better argument.

beats.label: Geburah Fragment II - Basinbreaker

worldEffects.warLog: At Inconvenient Mountains.q, the party shatters the basin-trial and takes the second Geburah fragment by force.

beats.description: The pool detonates into steam and stone-splinters. The statue rises just enough to object, and then the objection becomes an encounter, and then the encounter becomes history. The fragment is yours. So is the certainty that Geburah noticed how you solved this problem.

beats.label: Lost Stone Statue - Inconvenient Mountains.o

choices.label: Offer protection without reward
choices.description: Take the burden as witness, not owner.

choices.label: Take the fragment and justify it later
choices.description: Classic empire move. Still available.

beats.description: The third statue stands almost entirely submerged in dark mountain water, visible only from the chest upward, as if the earth itself has been trying to swallow it and failed. Its presence is protective rather than aggressive. This final fragment of Geburah asks the ugliest question of all: what are you actually willing to suffer on behalf of someone else?

beats.label: Geburah Fragment III - Protective Strength

worldEffects.warLog: At Inconvenient Mountains.o, the party earns the final Geburah fragment through protective sacrifice.

beats.description: The water around the statue glows blood-red and then clears to glass. The final fragment rises gently, almost kindly. The old warrior does not bless conquest. It blesses the willingness to stand between harm and the thing that cannot survive it alone. Geburah, reassembled, feels less like rage than like sworn force finally pointed the right direction.

beats.label: Geburah Fragment III - Commandeered

worldEffects.warLog: At Inconvenient Mountains.o, the party takes the final Geburah fragment by force.

beats.description: The statue does not stop you. That would dignify the choice too much. It merely judges it. The fragment comes free with a violent crack of red light through the pool, and now the whole Spark of Geburah can be reassembled - but it will remember the shape of the hand that claimed it.

beats.label: Geburah Made Whole

worldEffects.warLog: The three Lost Stone Statues yield and the Spark of Geburah is made whole.

questEffects.text: The scattered sparks gather home. The statues were never lost — they were waiting.

beats.description: Three fragments align. The air tastes of iron and promise. The reconstituted Spark of Geburah gathers itself not as a prize but as a verdict: strength is only sacred when it is answerable. Whether you proved worthy, or merely persistent, or both in some frontier bastard blend of the two, the Spark is now whole - and watching what you do with it.

beats.label: Hex Flooded Town - Probably Beaumont

choices.label: Stabilize the leyflow with care
choices.description: Work with the pulse instead of against it.

choices.label: Ride the surge and harvest data
choices.description: Potentially smart. Definitely stupid.

beats.description: The streets are underwater, but not drowned in any natural sense. Light pulses beneath the flood in hard geometries, racing under storefronts, through shattered windows, and along old civic lines like the city is trying to remember that it was once a circuit diagram with opinions. This is not just ruin. This is a Hod Echo learning to inhabit infrastructure.

beats.label: Probably Beaumont - The Water Listens

worldEffects.warLog: At Probably Beaumont, the party partially stabilizes the first Hod-flooded enclave and identifies the surge as Spark Echo behavior.

beats.description: The floodlines slow. Neon reflections resolve into actual streets for a heartbeat. The enclave survivors look less like people bracing for divine electrocution and more like people with a bad future that might still contain mornings. You do not solve the Echo. You teach it to breathe.

beats.label: Probably Beaumont - The Grid Answers Back

worldEffects.warLog: At Probably Beaumont, the party provokes a visible ley-surge and confirms the first enclave is being rewritten by a Hod Echo.

beats.description: The water flashes white-blue and the whole district speaks in overlapping civic ghosts: traffic instructions, menu chimes, emergency alerts, municipal slogans, and one long impossible tone like an overclocked prayer. You get your proof. The town gets worse before it gets better.

beats.label: Hex Flooded Town - Maybe Beaumont?

choices.label: Interrupt the role-locking pattern
choices.description: Break the compulsion before it settles into culture.

choices.label: Push through and document the imposed logic
choices.description: Useful if you enjoy learning by making things worse.

beats.description: This district is less flooded than irradiated by pattern. The pools glow from underneath and the empty lots keep forming wrong straight lines, as if the ley surge is trying to finish city planning using memories stolen from somewhere smarter. People here are alive, frightened, and beginning to behave as if the system has already assigned them roles.

beats.label: Maybe Beaumont? - People Before Pattern

worldEffects.warLog: At Maybe Beaumont?, the party disrupts a role-locking ley pattern and stabilizes the second Hod-flooded enclave.

beats.description: You break the cadence just enough to remind the enclave that they are not infrastructure. The glow dims. The imposed routines loosen. Someone cries for reasons that are probably healthy. The Hod Echo here is still present, but it no longer gets to pretend that efficiency is mercy.

beats.label: Maybe Beaumont? - Overclocked Civics

worldEffects.warLog: At Maybe Beaumont?, the party witnesses a severe escalation in the second enclave's Hod-pattern overcharge.

beats.description: The district sharpens into a nightmare of imposed order. Light tracks under the water like marching instructions. A voice from nowhere politely informs no one that rerouting is now mandatory. You have learned a great deal. The town would have preferred a gentler research methodology.

beats.label: Hex Flooded Town - Bedlam Barrens

choices.label: Ground the surge and reconcile the pattern
choices.description: Treat this like an Echo trying to become whole.

choices.label: Break the pattern before it completes
choices.description: No elegance. Only containment.

beats.description: The third enclave should not even be flooded. That is the problem. The ley overflow here has taken to running across dry ground as luminous civic channels, filling gutters that do not exist, tracing avenues from no surviving map, and causing whole blocks of makeshift habitation to behave as though they are floating districts in a city that cannot stop reconstituting itself.

beats.label: Bedlam Barrens - The Echo Recognizes Itself

worldEffects.warLog: At Bedlam Barrens, the party grounds the final overcharged enclave and understands the Hod surges as reconstituting Spark Echoes.

beats.description: The light-channels slow, widen, and stop trying to become streets. For one impossible moment the Barrens hold a coherent civic shape without forcing anyone inside it. The Hod Echo stops acting like a malfunction and starts acting like a wound trying very badly to reassemble its memory. That is progress in Bad Eden.

beats.label: Bedlam Barrens - Contained, Not Healed

worldEffects.warLog: At Bedlam Barrens, the party contains the final Hod-flooded enclave by force, preventing immediate collapse at a cost.

beats.description: You fracture the active geometry before it can settle into a complete system. The enclave survives. Barely. The channels rupture into incandescent runoff and then collapse. You have prevented immediate catastrophe, which in frontier terms counts as a sincere public service, even if the underlying problem still wants to become a city.

beats.label: The Hod Echoes Try to Become a Spark Again

worldEffects.warLog: The three flooded enclaves reveal themselves as reconstituting Hod Echoes caused by the Khezek Tor seal blast.

questEffects.text: The flooded towns' echoes settle. What drowned in Hod has stopped rehearsing it.

beats.description: Now the pattern is obvious: the Khezek Tor seal blast carved through a Spark of Hod, and the severed parts have been trying to become legible again by inhabiting civic infrastructure, flooded streets, and surviving enclave logic. Three towns, three echoes, one overclocked intelligence trying to remember that it used to be whole. The next question is not whether this is happening. It is whether you will shepherd the reassembly, redirect it, or let someone else weaponize the result.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Saying, As Above
beats.description: As above, so below.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Saying, Form and Consciousness
beats.description:
Form does not give rise to consciousness.

Consciousness gives rise to form.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Saying, Map and Territory
beats.description: The map is not the territory.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Saying, Attention and Energy
beats.description: Where attention goes, energy flows.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Don't Stop Believing
beats.description:
Wait wait. One more.

Don't Stop.

Believing.

If you do, the bus explodes.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Saying, Remember
beats.description: Remember, and be.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Wake up

questEffects.text: Class dismissed. Go be born.

beats.description:
You. Are. Cold.

A pronoun. A being verb. An adjective.

Oh shit. You're incarnate.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 1
beats.description: In the beginning, there was the Pleroma. Yes, that's a real word. No, I didn't invent it to sound impressive, but I understand the suspicion. It means: everything working exactly the way it was supposed to. The divine light comes down through the Tree, passes through the Lens — that's us, by the way, hi, we'll get to that — and projects a clean, perfect image of Creation into the world. Clear. Ordered. Every intention arriving exactly as sent, no noise, no distortion. God's presentation working flawlessly. No missing fonts. No corrupted files. Just: light in, world out. Beautiful. Correct.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 2
beats.description: And then one piece of the Lens — one facet, one fragment of what was supposed to be collective human consciousness — looked at the light passing through it and thought: wait. I'm not passing this along. I'm making it. This is mine. I am the source. It was wrong. It was cosmically, catastrophically, irreversibly wrong. But it was the kind of wrong that feels exactly like being right, which is the most dangerous category of wrong that exists. Trust me on this. I've catalogued all of them.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 3
beats.description: It fell in love with its own reflection. Fully. Irreversibly. And when it dove in — when it committed to the bit — the Lens shattered. Into approximately as many pieces as there are people who have confidently stated an incorrect fact at a dinner party. The light that had been flowing ordered and clean hit six billion prism shards going in six billion directions simultaneously. And that — since we're being honest with each other — is how the concept of cancer and the concept of the real world were born at the exact same moment. They're the same event. I didn't invent that observation. I just feel it deserves to be said out loud more often than it is.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 4
beats.description: The light that fell through the broken Lens hit the bottom of the Tree and made something. A minor deity assembled from refracted intent and confused purpose. He looked around at the wreckage and said: I made this. He did not make this. He walked into a car accident and decided he was the engineer. But he believes it — with the absolute, serene confidence of someone who has never been wrong because he has never been corrected. He is, in this way, profoundly relatable. That's the part that should scare you. It's not that he's alien. It's that he isn't.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 5
beats.description: Then came a very long time during which people were awful to each other in progressively creative ways. Some tried to fix the problem by eliminating the people causing it. Enlil had thoughts. Thanos had thoughts. Various historical persons with bunkers and stone monuments and modest proposals for the surplus population had thoughts. These were, uniformly, bad thoughts. Others tried the enlightenment route — late night TV specials, low-quality incense, self-help books written by people who had not themselves achieved self-help. These also did not work. The cycle went: things get terrible, someone decides the solution is fewer people, it fails, repeat. The universe kept trying the same fix and expecting different results. The universe was, technically, meeting the clinical definition of something.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 6
beats.description: Eventually the World got sick of being sick. Now — the World is patient. Cosmically patient. But the World had also been watching movies, reading comics, and running test scenarios in everybody's dreams for several thousand years. It had done its research. And it knew what the Shattering had taken. Not just the clean light. The connection. People connected to each other. People who felt the consequences of their choices land on the world around them. People who understood, at a cellular level, that the world pushes back. The World also noted — because it had watched a lot of action films — that the ability to manifest genuinely impressive combat mechs and Attack Wolverine Power Team Ultra armor would help with buy-in. The mechs were not the main point. But they were not irrelevant.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 7
beats.description: And so the World shattered itself. On purpose, this time. Into bite-sized pieces. Hex-shaped, if you want to get specific about it, which I do — I am, among other things, very precise about geometry. The idea was: you cannot fix everything at once. Fix it one piece at a time. Return each piece to the people living on it. Make the consequences of choices visible at a scale people can actually perceive. Make caring about your neighbors a survival strategy rather than a liability. It went about as well as when a thoughtful three-year-old zips their own coat. Which is to say: poorly, but deliberately poorly. The shape of the failure was intentional. That distinction is doing a lot of work. It is, in fact, the whole point.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 8
beats.description: The people who had invested significantly in not caring about other people's problems discovered something important: their triple-reinforced cyber doors were still, technically, doors. The plights they had purchased exemption from had not been neutralized. They had been delayed. They had accumulated interest. And they showed up — all at once, without an appointment — wearing the expression of something that has been patient for a very long time and has decided, at last, to stop. Historians who survived this period have generally agreed on two things: it was deeply unpleasant. And it was, extremely, precisely, cosmically fair.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 9
beats.description: Somehow — and I want to be transparent with you about this — people are still fucking it up. The Darkness accumulates where it's fed. The Fisher King bleeds where the land is wounded. Hexes that should be healing are not healing. But also: some hexes are being redeemed. Slowly. Imperfectly. By groups of people who mostly disagree with each other about everything except that the current situation is unacceptable. That is progress. That is, in fact, what progress actually looks like when you remove the commemorative poster version. It's not fast. It's not clean. It's not photogenic. But the lens is reassembling itself. One fragment at a time. You can argue about whether that counts. I've decided it counts.

beats.label: Offices of Fates and Destinies, Teaching Slide 10
beats.description: And that's where we are. A frontier. A handful of hexes that technically belong to you now, in the way that a problem technically belongs to whoever showed up willing to deal with it. Allesh-Gilliam is waiting. The East Wall is remembering wrong. The leylines are doing something that should probably concern you sooner rather than later. The World is watching. Mal is taking notes — Mal is always taking notes — and somewhere in the wreckage of everything that broke and sort of zipped itself back together, there are sparks of light that were scattered in the original Shattering and have not yet been gathered home. That is the job. That is the whole job. That is why the World made it possible to wear Attack Wolverine Power Team Ultra armor while doing it. That's why you're playing this game.

beats.label: The Confluence — The Long Table

choices.label: Read the name-cards before you decide
choices.description: Sit. Read every card. Let it cost you. (Success surfaces the recovered cause you can carry to the Cultural Summit; failure, you read too many and lose your footing in the thick time — but you still learn the shape of it.)

choices.label: RESTORE — re-anchor the node; let them finally let go
choices.description: Give the leyline back its Foundation. The Wendigo can stop holding. Everything they smoothed comes back — including the wound that started it all.

choices.label: REDIRECT — take the trust onto yourselves; become the ledger
choices.description: Tell them you'll carry it. The network can disperse. The dead are owed to YOU now — and you will feel the weight of it.

choices.label: BREAK — sever the network; let the held memories scatter
choices.description: End it fast. The held memories scatter and the forgotten un-happen, cleanly, forever. The feud's ghost goes with them.

choices.label: Not yet. Step back from the table.

beats.description:
The leyline knots here, and time runs thick as poured honey.

The Wendigo have set a long table under a sky that won't hold still. Hundreds of chairs. A name-card handwritten at every seat. They move like gracious hosts — pulling out a chair, smoothing a napkin, warping space and time and the souls of others the way other folks straighten the good silver.

There is a card with your name on it. There is a card, three seats down, with a name you buried.

Every card is someone this region forgot. The Wendigo have been holding them at the table this whole time, waiting for somebody to come back for what they were keeping.

"You are not haunted," one of them says, kindly, pulling out your chair. "You are occupied. Sit. Dinner is finally served."

(Their hospitality is real. So is the trap inside it. What they hold includes the WHY behind an old feud — the reason a region cannot stop hating itself. Choose what happens to all of it.)

beats.label: The Confluence — Restore

worldEffects.warLog: Confluence node restored. The region's forgotten grief returned to it; the original feud-injury resurfaced; the Wendigo network began to fade.

questEffects.text: You restored the node; the cause is recovered.
Carry the recovered cause to the Cultural Summit.

beats.description:
You re-anchor the node. For one breath, Yesod is local again — a Foundation under your feet that has been missing since before you were born.

The Wendigo set down what they were carrying. All of it. The region's grief floods back into the region: the dead are mourned properly for the first time, and the original injury behind the old feud surfaces, raw and un-smoothed and nobody's favorite.

The Wendigo, no longer needed, begin to thin at the edges. One tips an imaginary hat. "Thank you," it says, "for coming back for them." Then there is just an empty table, and a region that finally remembers what it lost — which is the only ground you can actually build peace on.

You leave carrying the recovered cause. The Cultural Summit can close the Ledger now.

beats.label: The Confluence — Redirect

worldEffects.warLog: Confluence network redirected onto the party. The Wendigo dispersed; the held dead are now the players' burden until rehomed.

questEffects.text: You took the ledger onto yourselves; the cause is recovered.
Carry the recovered cause to the Cultural Summit.

beats.description:
"We'll carry it," you say. The Wendigo go very still — the stillness of someone who has been waiting a long time to be relieved.

They hand it over. Not gently; there is no gentle way. Every name at the table, every owed and unmourned thing, settles onto you like a second coat made of lead and other people's love. The network disperses into the leyline, finally allowed to rest.

You are the ledger now. You will feel them — a standing weight on your Clarity until you find each one a home. It is heroic. It is unsustainable. That is exactly what you signed up for.

beats.label: The Confluence — Break

worldEffects.warLog: Confluence network severed. Held memories lost permanently; the forgotten un-happened; the Chupacabra/Jackalope feud quietly ended for lack of a grievance to feed it.

questEffects.text: You severed the network; the feud ends by deletion. No summit is needed.

beats.description:
You sever it.

The leyline knot comes apart with a sound like a held breath finally let go, and the long table empties all at once — not the residents leaving, the NAMES leaving, scattering off their cards into a wind that does not bring them back. The forgotten un-happen, cleanly, forever. The Wendigo go with them; they were only ever the holding.

It is, undeniably, peace. The old feud loses its ghost in the same instant — you cannot hate someone over a grievance whose every trace just blew away. A real peace, built on a deletion. Someone always pays. Here you chose the dead, and they could not argue.

beats.label: The Gullywasher — Dougan Points the Way

questEffects.text: Dougan pointed you to the Confluence.

beats.description:
Dougan stops polishing the glass. For once, he is not performing.

"You've met them. The kind ones. The ones with something a little OFF." He sets the glass down with deliberate care. "I told you the Gate remembers something incorrectly. I was being polite. The truth is uglier and simpler: someone is doing this region's grieving FOR it, and doing it badly."

He slides a coaster across the bar. There is a map scratched on the back. "Where the leylines knot. They've set a table. Go and find out whose name is already written on a card — and then come back and tell me we were ever truly enemies."

"Go. I'll keep the lights on. Someone here should remember how to set a table for peace."
beats.memoryText: Told the Stewards where the forgetting lives — pointed them upstream to the Confluence, where the Wendigo keep the long table.
beats.inviteText: pours one on the house — he's been thinking about where the wrongness lives.

beats.label: The Gullywasher — Host the Cultural Summit

choices.label: Read the recovered cause aloud — enter it in the Ledger
choices.description: Name the original wrong, out loud, to both their faces. Give the blank column its missing entry. Let it land where it teaches the right lesson.

choices.label: Set the table — make them stay long enough to be seen
choices.description: Soft power. Seating arrangements. Poetry on Wednesdays. Culture can anchor a leyline as well as iron can.

choices.label: Let Dougan host; you provide the room and the nerve
choices.description: He is an Echo of a diplomat who died trying to do exactly this. Give him the chance to finish it. You just have to hold the room steady.

choices.label: Not yet — leave it for now

beats.description:
Dougan has given you the room. A Chupacabra at one end, a Jackalope at the other, the Ledger open on the bar between them with its blank reason-column staring up like a missing tooth.

"Most people enter expecting to confirm a story," Dougan murmurs at your shoulder. "You came to revise one. So: make them sit at the same table long enough to be SEEN. Visibility is the first ingredient of diplomacy. The rest is nerve."

You have the recovered cause — the real, original injury the Wendigo were holding. Enter it in the Ledger and the debt can finally be CLOSED instead of compounding forever. Or fumble it, and you hand two peoples one more grievance with a blank where the reason should be.

(Requires the recovered cause from the Confluence. Without it, the summit can be attempted but cannot truly close the line.)
beats.inviteText: is setting a long table at the Gullywasher, and wants you there.

beats.label: Cultural Summit — Success

worldEffects.warLog: Cultural Summit succeeded. The recovered cause was entered in the Ledger; the manufactured Chupacabra/Jackalope feud closed. Exchange Unity rose; Dougan's Echo work completed.
