"Questions keep," she says, patting your arm. "Come by when you've slept. I find people decide better on the far side of a night's sleep. And I do like people who decide well."

beats.label: Lyrenn — Walking the Rows

choices.label: The Green Ring
choices.description: The town circle. Where Lyrenn talks TO itself, ABOUT itself, in front of itself. Radial farming and communal grievances.

choices.label: Meet Elsin Quade
choices.description: Keeper of the ledgers. A handshake like a soil report.

choices.label: Meet Rowan of the Loam
choices.description: Keeper of the listening. Do not expect them to hurry. The ground doesn't.

choices.label: Drink the well-water
choices.description: Cold. Clean. Faintly mineral. The fence post creaks in a way you'd swear was "you're welcome."

choices.label: Call it a day
choices.description: You sleep in a loft over the co-op. The chimes work the night shift. The land files you under: PENDING.

beats.description:
Lyrenn doesn't greet you. It notices you — which around here is the same thing, done more honestly.

The rows bend with the light. Wind chimes made from irrigation parts keep up their constant nervous music. Workers straighten as you pass, tip a tool, and go back to it: no ceremony, no suspicion, just a place with too much growing to stop for anybody.

Somebody has left a jug of cold well-water and two cups on a fence post along the main path. It was not there a minute ago. Nobody nearby takes credit.

The soil is dark, the air is sweet, and the whole hex is paying attention. Be worth paying attention to.

Who do you want to meet?

beats.label: Lyrenn — Supper at Elsin's Table

choices.label: Compliment the stew
choices.description: "It's food," she says. But the corner of her mouth files an exception.

choices.label: Offer to wash up
choices.description: She watches you dry each bowl like an auditor. You pass. PROBABLY.

beats.description:
Elsin Quade takes your measure over one firm handshake and zero wasted words. Then, verdict rendered, she does the most disarming thing available to her: she feeds you.

Her table is co-op plank, scrubbed pale. The meal is squash, bread, and a stew that doesn't need to explain itself. She serves you first — that's policy, not affection — and eats like a woman who has budgeted exactly enough time for eating and intends to hit the estimate. The ledger sits closed on the shelf. You get the sense that it being closed, in front of you, on your first night, is a statement of some kind.

"Farm feeds the town," she says, by way of grace. "Town holds the wall. Wall keeps the farm. That's the whole religion."

She refills your bowl without asking.

"Everything else is weather."

beats.label: Lyrenn — Rowan Introduces You to the Ground

choices.label: Ask what the rhythm is
choices.description: Rowan considers. "Growing," they decide, "is a sound, if you're patient." That is apparently the whole answer.

choices.label: Sit in the fallow row a while
choices.description: You and Rowan do nothing together, expertly, until sundown. This is — and you'd fight anyone who said otherwise — one of the ten best meetings of your life.

beats.description:
You find Rowan of the Loam standing in a fallow row, doing nothing at all, doing it with total commitment.

They study you like a half-remembered dream. Then they crouch, press one palm flat to the soil, and gesture — unhurried, unmistakable — for you to do the same.

The ground is warm where it should be cool. Under the warmth, very faint, a rhythm. Not a heartbeat. More like breathing heard through a wall.

"It likes to know the weight of new people," Rowan says. "Now it knows yours."

They straighten up and give you the rarest thing in Bad Eden: a smile with nothing behind it but the smile.

"Welcome to Lyrenn. Walk gently the first week. It notices manners."

beats.label: Khezek Tor — A Seat at the Cookline

choices.label: Eat what Bez gives you
choices.description: You will never learn what it was. You will dream about it anyway. Bez nods once — the full Khezek Tor citizenship ceremony.

choices.label: Meet Drax Calder
choices.description: The foreman. He'll talk while he works. He never stops working.

choices.label: Meet Sable Nine
choices.description: The mapmaker. Keeps their maps folded like secrets, because they are.

choices.label: Listen to the fiddle
choices.description: Three songs. All arguably the same song. The mountain hums under it, one register too low, like a very large uncle joining the chorus.

choices.label: Call it a day
choices.description: You bunk in a container barrack. It is EXACTLY as comfortable as it sounds — and somehow you're out in minutes. The mountain rocks nobody to sleep. And yet.

beats.description:
You hear Khezek Tor before you see it. A low, constant vibration — stone grinding against memory. Floodlights burning day and night. Not for visibility. For warning.

But at the shift change, the mountain shows you its other face: the cookline.

A welded row of drum-stoves at the mine's mouth, run by a granite-armed cook named Bez who does not take requests and has never needed to. Miners come up gray, eat, and turn back into people by the third bite. A place gets made for you on the bench — no discussion, someone just shoves down and it exists.

Tin plate. Real portions. Somebody's fiddle, played badly, loved anyway.

Nobody asks what you're going to do about anything. Down here, showing up at the cookline IS the introduction.

beats.label: Khezek Tor — Calder Talks While He Works

choices.label: Drink the miner's coffee
choices.description: It stands up to the spoon. Possibly to a pickaxe. Your ancestors — ALL of them — feel this one.

choices.label: Ask about the chalk marks
choices.description: "Chalk's cheap," Calder says. "Surprises aren't." He's watching the marks while he says it, so you know it's the closest thing he has to a lullaby.

beats.description:
Drax Calder doesn't shake hands — his are full. Chalk in one, level in the other, and a length of the Brace in front of him that he treats the way other people treat a sleeping animal.

"New watch," he says. Not a question. Word beat you down the mountain.

He keeps working while he talks, and what he talks about is the shift: who's on it, who's new, whose kid just moved from sorting to carting and got cheered down the whole line. The ledger behind him is rock, chalk, and arithmetic older than the coalition — every line somebody's shift, somebody's tonnage, somebody's name.

"You'll want to know the mine eventually," he says, tapping a chalk mark back into true. "The mine'll want to know you first. That part takes exactly as long as it takes."

He hands you a cup of the tar the miners call coffee.

"Tonight, you're a guest. Guests eat first and stay off the lifts. Both rules are load-bearing."

beats.label: Khezek Tor — Sable Nine, at a Polite Distance

choices.label: Take the good seat
choices.description: The draft misses you entirely. Sable, not looking up, almost smiles. You have been ENTERED INTO THE RECORD.

choices.label: Ask what they're mapping
choices.description: "The mine," says Sable, in the tone of someone answering a different question than the one you asked. The folded map stays folded.

beats.description:
Sable Nine has claimed the end of the bench nearest the light, folded over a map like a bird over an egg.

You get one eye. Then the other. The map, you notice, gets folded FIRST — before the greeting, before anything.

"You're the new watch," they say quietly. "You walk loud. That's not a criticism. It's data."

Up close, Sable is all economy: charcoal fingers, careful voice, the stillness of somebody who spends whole shifts listening to rock. They do not show you the maps. They do show you the good seat — back to the wall, view of the mouth, where the draft doesn't reach. In Sable Nine terms this is roughly a bouquet of flowers.

"Sit there when you visit," they say. "I'll know it's you without looking up. That saves us both a little."

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm — Open for Browsing

choices.label: The Gullywasher
choices.description: There's a bar! The bartender situation is... look, just go see the bartender situation.

choices.label: Browse the yard
choices.description: Rig parts, salvage sorted with terrifying precision, and a bin labeled MYSTERY (AS IS, NO REFUNDS, STOP ASKING). You do not buy the mystery. The mystery will keep.

choices.label: Call it a day
choices.description: You bed down in the caravan loft. The chimes never fully stop. Neither, you suspect, does the math.

beats.description:
Up close, the corpse that refused to lie down turns out to be extremely alive: generators humming, chimes clattering their endless key-and-casing argument, and a hand-painted OPEN sign with three exclamation points — one of which was clearly added later, in different paint. Somebody here believes in customer service. Somebody else here fixed the first somebody's spelling. (It used to say OPNE.)

A Jackalope kid — Pip, or possibly Patter — materializes at your elbow, walks you exactly one lap of the yard, points out the Gullywasher ("bar"), the Counter ("closed till Mara says"), Arc Bay ("LOUD later"), and the Generator hall ("escort only, it's not personal"), accepts no questions, and vanishes on the half-hop.

Best first-day tour you've ever had, honestly.

beats.label: Furrier's Fixit Farm — First Round's Cultural

choices.label: Drink the amber thing
choices.description: It tastes like peaches that did something unforgivable and got away with it. You'd order another, but your eyebrows are still filing their report.

choices.label: Ask his name
choices.description: "Behind the bar? Gully." A glass gets polished. "Everywhere else — we'll see if you earn it."

beats.description:
There is a Chupacabra standing behind the bar, washing glasses. Oh shit — he's the bartender.

That was not on your post-apocalyptic 5D bingo card this morning.

He clocks your face doing the thing every new face does, gives it precisely two seconds of patience, and slides a glass down the bar. Something amber. Something carbonated, aggressively.

"House rule," he says. The accent is pure ranch country. "First one's on the Farm. Second one, you tell me where you're from. Third one, I tell you where I'M from, and you buy THAT round, because it's a better story."

Around you: Jackalopes off shift, a teamster asleep sitting up with a full glass in hand (nobody touches it), and a dartboard where the bullseye has been relabeled ANYWHERE. The Gullywasher, it turns out, is exactly what it looks like: the one room in the wasteland where everybody's from somewhere else, and that's the whole point.

beats.label: The Tent at the Edge of Town
beats.description: Someone has put up a tent at the edge of the settlement — white canvas, guyed out square, so clean it looks subtracted from the landscape rather than added to it. Inside: cots, all made. A woman changes water in a basin nobody is using. She is kind to you in a completely unremarkable way, answers everything you ask, and volunteers nothing. On the walk back somebody in your party says the thing out loud: this town used to be LOUD. You were here — what, a season ago? There were dogs. There was an argument about a fence that everyone in earshot had opinions about. Nobody can tell you when it stopped. Nobody seems to have noticed it stopping. The fence is still there, and the argument is not.

beats.label: Travelers Who Won't Eat
beats.description: Two of them, on the road, on foot, immaculate — which out here is the strangest thing a person can be. No dust past the ankle. They know the courtesies, all of them, in the right order, and they use your name back to you correctly the first time. They pay for the meal. They pay OVER, cheerfully, waving off change. And then they do not eat it: the bowls sit cooling in front of them for the entire conversation, and at the end they thank the cook for it, specifically and warmly, and leave it exactly as it came. They ask after your dead. Not morbidly — the way you'd ask after somebody's knee. They seem genuinely glad to hear the number.

beats.label: The Post with the Tally on It
beats.description: It's a waypost, and the tally cut into it is old enough that the newest marks have weathered grey. Someone maintains this. The wood's been oiled where the numbers are. And the numbers only ever go DOWN — you can read the sequence backward down the post, each figure smaller than the one above it, no additions anywhere, no corrections, the arithmetic of something being carefully and patiently subtracted from over a very long time. The most recent cut is not recent. Whatever it was counting either finished, or got small enough that counting stopped being the point.

beats.label: The Meeting Under the Big Canvas
beats.description: The tent holds three hundred and the town holds eighty, and yet here we all are. It's a good meeting — genuinely, annoyingly good; the singing is excellent and the food is free and abundant and the welcome is so total that you're four songs deep before the arithmetic lands. Nobody here is FROM here. You ask a man where he's traveled in from and he looks pleased and a little puzzled, like you've asked him what color the alphabet is, and says he's been coming for years. Everyone is delighted. Everyone is new. Somebody presses a second helping on you and will not be argued out of it.

beats.label: She Already Knew How
beats.description: She came back three months ago — an ordinary resolution, the kind the hexes do when they're settled and well-tended, nothing anybody would remark on. Except she came back knowing a trade. Not remembering one: KNOWING one, hands-first, the whole grammar of it, well enough that the smith has stopped correcting her and started watching. Asked who taught her, she gives you a completely open face and says she doesn't know, and you can tell it's not evasion, it's the actual answer. It doesn't distress her. It distresses the smith, who has been doing this for thirty years and had to be taught.

beats.label: The House the Kudzu Wrote On
beats.description: The kudzu has taken the whole southern wall, which is normal, and gone in through the window and out through the roof, which is also normal, and made a shape on the way that is not. From the road it's just growth. From up the slope, at the wrong time of afternoon, with the light across it, the vine on that wall runs in long connected loops with consistent spacing and a consistent slant, and the word your brain reaches for before you can stop it is CURSIVE. It doesn't spell anything. You check. It doesn't spell anything in any alphabet anyone in the party can read, and it keeps not spelling anything for as long as you stand there looking at it, which is longer than you meant to.

beats.label: The Thin Sour Honey
beats.description: It's nothing like the honey you know: thin as syrup, faintly sour, faintly citric, and it will not behave in a spoon. The instruction that came with it was four words long and delivered without ceremony — a drop in each eye. It stings for exactly as long as it takes to regret it. And then, over about a day, the world sharpens: the swim goes out of distance, the grit-ache of a decade of wind and glare and reading by bad light quietly stops being a fact of your face. Nobody offers a theory. The person who gave it to you seemed to think the honey was the boring part.
beats.memoryText: A jar of thin, sour honey, dripped in the eyes, measurably improved someone's sight. No explanation was offered or, apparently, available.

beats.label: Somebody Has to Tell Them
beats.description: The hives are behind the house, six of them, older than the house. When the news reaches her she does not sit down and she does not cry — she picks up a strip of black cloth that is clearly kept for this, walks out back, and tells the bees. Out loud. In full sentences, with the name in them, and the date, and how it happened, the way you'd report to somebody who has a right to know and has been away. Then she ties the cloth to the nearest hive and stands there a moment in case there's a reply. On the way back in she tells you, without any particular emphasis, that if you don't tell them they leave. ⚠ GM: the bee-teller is an NPC MINT (owner action). Per the ladder she is Tier 2, DOABLE — the payload is that the party must tell her when one of THEM dies.
beats.memoryText: A woman formally informed her beehives of a death, in full sentences, and tied black cloth to the hive. She says that if you don't tell them, they leave.

beats.label: Classification Review
beats.description: The flag traveled faster than you did. Days after the parley, a verification pack crested the ridge line behind you — modular bikes in a spread formation, one crawler-rig running with its panel open. They were not hiding. They never are. A speaker crackled across the distance: “CITIZENS. YOUR CLASSIFICATION IS UNDER REVIEW. PLEASE MAINTAIN CURRENT VELOCITY.” Maintaining current velocity has never once been the plan.

choices.label: Hold position and stand the audit
choices.description: Zero lag between recognizing the situation and acting like you recognized it.

choices.label: Ride
choices.description: Their network is fast. Are you faster?

beats.label: Eleven Minutes of Dignity
beats.description: You held position while the pack circled and scanned. It took eleven minutes and cost nothing but composure. Simone rode past last, slow, and looked at you the way an auditor looks at a ledger that unexpectedly balances: no lag. The classification did not change. The tone of it did.

worldEffects.warLog: Stood a Circuit Rider classification review without running. Simone logged zero lag.

beats.label: The Riders Do Not Stop Twice
beats.description: You did not maintain current velocity. The pack folded off the ridge in eerie coordination, route-prediction overlays already guessing at your next three turns. From the crawler-rig's open panel, someone sounded genuinely delighted.

beats.label: Arrived Where You Were Always Going To Be
beats.description: The crawler-rig did not overtake you so much as arrive where you were always going to be. The pack boxed politely — no weapons, just angles. Captain Robot's voice came through the speaker, unhurried: verification first. The review happened on the roadside, engines idling. They logged your evasion pattern, thanked you for the data, and left the classification standing. Somewhere behind the formation, something enormous shifted its weight and settled.

worldEffects.warLog: Ran from a Circuit Rider classification review; caught. Evasion pattern logged.

beats.label: Faster Than the Apology
beats.description: You beat the prediction — through geometry their models refuse to route through, across water their wheels cannot hold. The pack broke off without drama; theatrical pursuit is not doctrine. That night, a relay tower you had passed clicked once, twice, and went quiet. The classification stands. The network is faster than your apology, and now it has your top speed.

worldEffects.warLog: Outran a Circuit Rider verification pack. Classification stands; top speed logged.

quest_Cq1v3hJpXarX5rXJ.name: Allesh-Gilliam
quest_Cq1v3hJpXarX5rXJ.description:
Wow. You're in charge of three hexes. What was ANYONE thinking, including you? Might as well take a look around ...

Seriously though WOW ...

quest_nrkJabUwZOLAJFYn.name: Furrier's Fixit Farm
quest_nrkJabUwZOLAJFYn.description: You need a Leyline stabilizer. The folks at the Fixit Farm have one, for the right price. Best go check it out!

quest_JqCdOo0l6X8K2EcE.name: Lyrenn
quest_JqCdOo0l6X8K2EcE.description: Farm to Bunker! The Water Choir is supposed to be worth the price of admission alone. And you don't have to pay ANYTHING!

quest_LJAmlim7oUtlMPiC.name: Khezek Tor
quest_LJAmlim7oUtlMPiC.description: A recently restarted mining operation. Because mining oprrations that were mysteriously and hurriedly shut down are the kinds of things that need to be started back up again. If nothing else just to see what the fuck happens! I'LL SHOW YOU DELVED TOO DEEP OR WHATEVER!

quest_uDuNp2yQxbuKkHx7.name: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Weeping Prisoner
quest_uDuNp2yQxbuKkHx7.description: A local was caught stealing, and now sits in chains in the Arc Bay, awaiting justice.

quest_uMKbX648SllKTpEH.name: Lyrenn - The Gentle Pest
quest_uMKbX648SllKTpEH.description:
A swarm of small, root-burrowing creatures is destroying irrigation channels.
They flee from tools. They stop when spoken to kindly.

quest_0HBaQXGlhFvNke2B.name: Lyrenn - The Field That Remembers You
quest_0HBaQXGlhFvNke2B.description:
A low field near Lyrenn has begun growing plants shaped like people’s regrets.
Not statues — gestures. Bent shoulders. Clutching hands. Faces turned away from something they should have said.

quest_feX6WHsBXuVbtjMM.name: Lyrenn - The Forest Will Not Be Fought
quest_feX6WHsBXuVbtjMM.description:
Lyrenn formally asks the PCs to mediate with the forest, not defend the town from it.

The forest is expanding — but not aggressively. Roads subtly move. Clearings reappear elsewhere.

quest_A050y4VtoZFzOfGz.name: Khezek Tor - The Mine that Answered Back
quest_A050y4VtoZFzOfGz.description:
A new mining shaft broke into something Qliphothic-adjacent.
Not a monster — a pressure.

Miners report the rock leaning in.

quest_2Gs2dsKhv7G1OYBl.name: Khezek Tor - The Shipment of UTTER DARKNESS Sometimes
quest_2Gs2dsKhv7G1OYBl.description:
Ore shipments from Khezek Tor cause Darkness spikes when mishandled.
Not cursed — improperly respected.

quest_AL1aIXiljxPUBH2e.name: Khezek Tor - The Valhaulan Seal
quest_AL1aIXiljxPUBH2e.description:
A sealed shaft bears Valhaulan markings.
They are recent.

quest_bSwOIWzxqNBwJ5NM.name: Furrier's Fixit Farm - The Leyline Stabilizer
quest_bSwOIWzxqNBwJ5NM.description: That thing that AJ did wiuth the Leygate was AWESOME.Unfortunately, you can't easily replicate that. Nor can you use it to set up travel to new hexes. Probably should fix that. Thankfully, you know some Jackrabbits who might have one for the right price!

quest_5obLcPkexYRVZqlg.name: Gloomgill - He that was Oannes
quest_5obLcPkexYRVZqlg.description:
“Something big lives in the water.
Something old.
Keeps coming back worse.”

People lower their voices when they say the name.
That’s never a good sign.

quest_2pZmPy9TEzorMoaj.name: The Forest of Early Tifaret
quest_2pZmPy9TEzorMoaj.description: In which a ding dang tree gets aggressive with therapy.

quest_NwiADv8ZDoklqwEJ.name: The Maneuver Vault
quest_NwiADv8ZDoklqwEJ.description: Pip is missing. Patter is going nuts. Pip went to the newly discovered Vault, and didn't come back. He always comes back. ALWAYS. But this time, he didn't.

quest_8II4GEGV7D3RgzPv.name: The Balcones Faulting You Line
quest_8II4GEGV7D3RgzPv.description:
The Balcones Fault is feeling a bit stressed. It feels like it's slipping. Like it wants to strike.

Tectonic pun.

quest_hidden_vault.name: The Hidden Vault
quest_hidden_vault.description: A mysterious bunker in the woods, holding ancient secrets of unknown provenance. Or monsters. Or ancient secret monsters. The word combinations are endless.

quest_forgotten_yesterdays.name: The Mall of Forgotten Yesterdays
quest_forgotten_yesterdays.description: Enter the haunted strip mall, navigate the Tanneritos, survive the hazards, and decide whether the mall becomes a relationship, a resource, or a cautionary tale.

quest_circuit_riders_parley.name: Circuit Rider Parley
quest_circuit_riders_parley.description: Make first contact with Captain Robot and the Circuit Riders, survive their verification rituals, and determine whether this becomes alliance, surveillance, or strategic distrust.

quest_thatwards_ho_finale.name: Thatwards Ho! Finale
quest_thatwards_ho_finale.description: Reach the Valhaulan bunker, secure the Yesodic Spark, uncover the truth of Monodynamic's redirection of Khezek Tor's energies, and determine whether the Valhaulans become allies, enemies, or merely another unstable force in Bad Eden.

quest_ycEa0uXzTzsbK4qP.name: Offices of Fates and Destinies
quest_ycEa0uXzTzsbK4qP.description: Intro to the whole thing! Free quest achievement! Act now!

fc_wendigo_confluence.name: Something a Little Off
fc_wendigo_confluence.description: The Wendigo along the leylines keep giving directions — and taking something you can't quite name. Find the long table where they hold what the region forgot, and decide what to do with it.

fc_cultural_summit.name: Close the Ledger
fc_cultural_summit.description: You carry the recovered cause of an ancient feud. Bring it to Dougan's Cultural Summit at the Gullywasher and enter it in the Ledger — reconcile the Chupacabras and Jackalopes for good.

quest_ag_town_militia.name: Allesh-Gilliam — The Town Militia
quest_ag_town_militia.description: Freed bandits plus a nervous town equals a militia. The Muster is open, Captain Brakk is drilling farmers, and Allesh-Gilliam is learning the difference between a wall and the people on it.

quest_ag_confessors_debt.name: Allesh-Gilliam — The Confessor's Debt
quest_ag_confessors_debt.description: Someone at St Gilliam's is keeping the mountain's new tenants informed. The candles know. The drip tray knows. The question the town taught you is coming back with the confessor's own face on it: what does justice look like?

quest_lyrenn_red_thread.name: Lyrenn — The Red Thread
quest_lyrenn_red_thread.description: Seeds gathered where the standing stones went quiet, planted where the one stone figure kneels. Lyrenn is counting mornings.

quest_lyrenn_land_remembers.name: Lyrenn — The Land Remembers
quest_lyrenn_land_remembers.description: Lyrenn does not punish violence immediately. It remembers it. The bill arrives later, politely, in the handwriting of the soil.

quest_kt_sink_watch.name: Khezek Tor — The Sink Watch
quest_kt_sink_watch.description: The opened deep is becoming a doorway, patiently. Sable charts its edges nightly and has started noting which direction the stone figures face.

quest_kt_compound_cough.name: Khezek Tor — The Compound Cough
quest_kt_compound_cough.description: The illness that came with doubled output. Calder keeps the list of names; Greeley keeps the folder marked OWED. Somebody, eventually, keeps the promise.

quest_kt_brace_strain.name: Khezek Tor — The Brace Strain
quest_kt_brace_strain.description: The Brace took the extra load without a word. The mountain has since cleared its throat. If it fails, the hex changes. Permanently.

quest_ninth_guest.name: The Ninth Guest
quest_ninth_guest.description: The Garden holds ninety-nine. The rite held one hundred. Somewhere in the world there is a guest who pays exact, keeps vigil instead of sleeping, and leaves no readable name — and somewhere on the Static Coast there is a plinth with feet-marks walking away from it. This question does not close quickly. It may not close in this age.

quest_bandit_accord.name: The Bandit Accord
quest_bandit_accord.description: The party keeps sparing bandits, and the Drowned South keeps count. Word travels through the reeds; the spared loiter near the Muster looking employable; ambushes start surrendering before the roll. Somewhere out past the stilt-camps, a Bandit Lord is bleeding personnel to your mercy — and arithmetic like that eventually writes a letter. How this ends (banner, muster, boot, or nothing) is up to the summit.

quest_cadence.name: The Cadence
quest_cadence.description: A crew that raids culturally: speakers, sequins, and a formal declaration of rhythm, delivered on cardstock. Losing to them costs face, not walls — and the story spreads to every neighboring hex. They have never thrown a punch. They have never needed to. Answer the declaration on the floor, or live with what the silence says about you.

quest_fifteen_year_siege.name: The Fifteen-Year Siege
quest_fifteen_year_siege.description: A coastal hex has been under siege for fifteen years, and the siege has tenure: the besiegers' children were born in the trench and go to school in the counterweight tower; the besieged run a farmers' market ON the wall on alternating Thursdays, which the siege observes, because everyone observes market day. Neither side remembers the original demand — the paperwork was lost in year three, and both commanders have quietly agreed that checking would be worse. The one thing they both fear is it actually ENDING. End it anyway. Or don't. There are at least four ways through, and one of them is a festival.

quest_siege_festival.name: Siege Week (Annual)
quest_siege_festival.description: The siege was chartered: a PROTECTED CULTURAL INSTITUTION, conducted ceremonially for one week a year, with rules, referees, historical costume, and a closing feast on the wall. Both sides got what they actually wanted, which was the routine. This quest stands open as long as the festival tradition lives — it is not a problem to solve; it is a calendar to keep.

quest_trojan_gift.name: A Gift. (Not a Trojan.)
quest_trojan_gift.description: An enormous gift has arrived at the gate, conspicuously, insultingly trojan-shaped. The label says it is NOT a trojan. Everyone knows the story; the sender clearly knows everyone knows; the town has started a betting pool (the Vacancy runs the book, of course). The actual game is nested: whatever you expect inside is the decoy. Accept it, inspect it, refuse it — or, in the great tradition of this coast, RE-GIFT it and let it be somebody else's parable.

quest_touring_gift.name: The Touring Gift
quest_touring_gift.description: The gift was re-gifted — forwarded to another faction with a new card attached — and the coast's strangest object is now IN CIRCULATION. It tours the map on the turn ticks, a diplomatic hot potato of growing legend, and at every stop its inventory gains exactly one more layer than the manifest admits. This quest stands open as long as the gift keeps moving. Nobody is sure what happens if it stops.

quest_valhaulan_spine.name: The Valhaulan Spine
quest_valhaulan_spine.description: The Story Director's main-arc chain: five bridge beats that stitch Khezek Tor's seal to the sky. Container quest so the spine is visible to quest-mode tools; the Director still drives firing.

quest_travel_encounters.name: Travel & Wandering Encounters
quest_travel_encounters.description: Container for the repeatable travel/wandering encounter suites (enc_*, acid bog, tag-injected events). Ambient content — not a narrative questline.

quest_thatwards_opening.name: Thatward's Ho — Opening
quest_thatwards_opening.description: The bus, the sendoff, the town below: the campaign's cold open and opening scene, fired by the Offices' incarnation closer.
